proposals.title: vn-number-format: formatNumber throws for maxFractionDigits outside 0–100 and garbles |n| ≥ 1e21
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `formatNumber` passes `opts.maxFractionDigits` straight to `Math.abs(n).toFixed(digits)`:
- `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })` (or `-1`, or `1.5`) throws `RangeError: toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100`. This breaks the library contract ("Every function returns `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }` — no exceptions for bad input", README.md).
- For `|n| >= 1e21`, `toFixed` returns exponent notation (`"1e+21"`). The grouping regex then produces a malformed string instead of `1.000.000.000.000.000.000.000`. `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` inherit both problems.

## Fix
- Validate `maxFractionDigits`: an integer in 0–20 (or 0–100), otherwise `fail('INVALID_OPTION', …)` with a hint naming the allowed range.
- For finite numbers whose `toFixed` output contains `e`, either format the integer part via `BigInt(Math.trunc(n))` or return `fail('INVALID_NUMBER', …)` with a clear message. Document the chosen behaviour in the JSDoc and in `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })`, `-1` and `1.5` return `ok: false` and do not throw
- [ ] `formatNumber(1e21)` returns either a correctly grouped string or `ok: false`, never a string containing `e`
- [ ] Golden cases added to `tests/golden/` for vn-number-format (the file loaded by `tests/golden.ts`), plus `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cases for the throwing inputs
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
proposals.rationale: Breaks the library's documented no-throw contract. Library callers can crash the process with an option value.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts formatNumber (toFixed call)","README.md#library (no exceptions for bad input)","$ formatNumber(1,{maxFractionDigits:101}) -> THROW toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100"]

proposals.title: vn-number-format: formatDate rejects valid years 0001–0099
proposals.body:
## Problem
`formatDate` in `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts` builds the date with `new Date(Date.UTC(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d))`. `Date.UTC` maps years 0–99 to 1900–1999, so the `getUTCFullYear() !== m.y` check fails, and `formatDate('0050-01-01')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_DATE', message: '"0050-01-01" is not a real calendar date' } }`. The regexes accept 4-digit years and the output pads to 4 digits (`p(m.y, 4)`), so these years are meant to work. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `date`) and the CLI `numfmt date` have the same problem.

## Fix
Build the date with `const dt = new Date(0); dt.setUTCFullYear(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d);` (or equivalent) so years below 100 are not remapped. Keep the existing validity check.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatDate('0050-01-01')` → `01/01/0050`
- [ ] `formatDate('29/02/0004')` → `29/02/0004` (leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar); `formatDate('0003-02-29')` → `INVALID_DATE`
- [ ] Existing behaviour for 4-digit years ≥ 1000 unchanged
- [ ] Cases added to the vn-number-format golden fixture in `tests/golden/`
proposals.rationale: Valid inputs are reported as impossible dates. A one-line fix with golden cases.

proposals.title: vn-number-format: parseAmount and formatDate throw on non-string input instead of returning an error
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `parseAmount` calls `input.toLowerCase()` and `formatDate` calls `input.trim()` without coercing the input. Untyped callers (plain JS, JSON from other tools) get exceptions:
- `parseAmount(5)` → `TypeError: input.toLowerCase is not a function`
- `formatDate(null)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'trim')`

Other modules already guard with `String(input ?? '')` (`parsePhone`, `validateTaxId`, `parseCitizenId`), and the README promises no exceptions for bad input.

## Fix
Start both functions with `const raw = String(input ?? '')` (keep the `string` parameter type). Numbers then parse naturally (`parseAmount(5)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`), and `null`/`undefined` return `INVALID_AMOUNT`/`INVALID_DATE`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount(5 as any)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`; `parseAmount(null as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `formatDate(null as any)` and `formatDate(20250101 as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_DATE`, no throw
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cover these cases
proposals.rationale: The numfmt functions are the only ones in the library that throw on bad input types. Aligning them with the other modules is trivial.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts parseAmount/formatDate","packages/core/src/phone, taxid, id use String(input ?? '')","$ parseAmount(5) -> THROW input.toLowerCase is not a function"]

proposals.title: vn-number-format: explain why amounts like "1.5" are rejected
proposals.body:
## Problem
`vn-skills numfmt parse "1.5"` returns `{ code: 'INVALID_AMOUNT', message: 'Cannot parse amount "1.5"', hint: 'Try "1tr2", "500k", "1.200.000"' }`. The rejection is intended: in `plainNumber` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`), `.` is a thousands separator only when every group has 3 digits, and `,` is the decimal mark. But the message does not say so, and users and agents typing the English decimal `1.5` do not know what to change. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `parse`) returns the same error.

## Fix
In `parseAmount`, when the numeric part contains `.` and fails the 3-digit grouping rule, return a specific hint: `"." groups thousands in Vietnamese (1.500 = 1500); use "," for decimals, e.g. "1,5"`. Keep the error code `INVALID_AMOUNT`. Other failures keep the current hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount('1.5')` and `parseAmount('1.50tr')` → `INVALID_AMOUNT` with a hint that mentions `,` as the decimal mark
- [ ] `parseAmount('abc')` keeps the existing hint
- [ ] `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md` common-mistakes section mentions this case
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts`
proposals.rationale: This error was the confusing one a newcomer hit while trying the CLI. A specific hint lets agents fix the input themselves.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts plainNumber/parseAmount","$ vn-skills numfmt parse \"1.5\" -> INVALID_AMOUNT with generic hint"]

proposals.title: docs: make the README einvoice example runnable and fix the in-repo CLI invocation
proposals.body:
## Problem
1. The README.md and README.vi.md skills tables show `vn-skills einvoice totals invoice.json`, but no step creates `invoice.json`, so a newcomer gets `READ_ERROR: Cannot read invoice JSON from invoice.json: ENOENT`. `vn-skills einvoice example` (`packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts`) prints a starter invoice, but the README never mentions it.
2. README.md says "Inside this repository (before the packages are published) use `pnpm vn-skills …`". The packages are published now. The pnpm wrapper (`package.json` script `"vn-skills": "node packages/cli/dist/index.js"`) echoes the command line, and on every `ok:false` result it appends `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.` after the JSON, even with `pnpm -s`. That breaks clean JSON for agents. Running `node packages/cli/dist/index.js …` directly is clean.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The einvoice example in both READMEs becomes `vn-skills einvoice example > invoice.json && vn-skills einvoice totals invoice.json` (keep the table readable; a footnote is fine)
- [ ] The in-repo note in both READMEs drops "before the packages are published", recommends `node packages/cli/dist/index.js …` for clean JSON, and mentions that `pnpm vn-skills` adds wrapper output
- [ ] Same change in CONTRIBUTING.md if it still recommends `pnpm vn-skills` for scripted use (keeping it for `--help` is fine)
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes (update it if it checks these lines)
proposals.rationale: Both are the friction a newcomer hit while trying the README. Each costs a first-time user a failed command.
proposals.evidence: ["README.md line 32 and 61","README.vi.md line 32 and 59","package.json scripts.vn-skills","packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts (example command)","$ pnpm -s vn-skills vietqr build --bank XXX --account 1 -> JSON + [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1."]

proposals.title: repo: fix the release token so 0.5.0 is tagged and published to npm
proposals.body:
## Problem
The 0.5.0 release commit (606314fe, #98) is on main, but npm still serves 0.4.0 as `latest` for `@vn-skills/core`, `@vn-skills/cli` and `@vn-skills/mcp`, and the newest GitHub Release is v0.4.0. In Release workflow run 39784434188 (2026-10-22 13:09 UTC), the release-please step failed with `release-please failed: Resource not accessible by integration` when it tried to create the release. The publish job was then skipped.

So #97, #99, #100, #101, the `vietqr_decode` MCP tool (#84) and `mcpName` (#103) have not reached users. The MCP Registry listing is blocked until this ships.

The workflow uses `AGENT_GITHUB_TOKEN` when it is set, otherwise `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The token probably lacks `contents: write` for releases.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Check which token the release job uses and give it permission to create tags and releases (`contents: write`), or switch the release step to a token that has it
- [ ] Re-run the Release workflow, or use its `workflow_dispatch` recovery path, so the `v0.5.0` tag and GitHub Release are created
- [ ] Confirm that `https://registry.npmjs.org/@vn-skills/mcp/latest` shows `0.5.0` and contains `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"`
- [ ] Confirm that `@vn-skills/core` and `@vn-skills/cli` are also at 0.5.0
- [ ] Optional: note the `ubuntu-latest` → Ubuntu 26 warning from the same run and decide whether to pin the runner image
proposals.rationale: [needs you] Merged fixes and the new MCP tool are not on npm, where all 2,100+ monthly downloads come from. Every listing step depends on this.

proposals.title: mcp: publish @vn-skills/mcp to the official MCP Registry once 0.5.0 is on npm
proposals.body:
## Problem
`packages/mcp/server.json` and `mcpName` landed in #103. The registry still returns `count: 0` for `vn-skills` (2026-10-22). The registry checks npm ownership by reading `mcpName` from the **published** `package.json`. 0.4.0 has no `mcpName`, so publishing fails until 0.5.0 is on npm.

Depends on the release-token issue (0.5.0 must be on npm first).

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Confirm that `https://registry.npmjs.org/@vn-skills/mcp/latest` is 0.5.0 and has `mcpName: io.github.beiryu/vn-skills`
- [ ] Confirm that the version in `packages/mcp/server.json` matches the published version
- [ ] From `packages/mcp`: `mcp-publisher login github`, then `mcp-publisher publish`
- [ ] Confirm that `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=vn-skills` returns the server
proposals.rationale: [needs you] MCP clients and aggregators read this registry. It is the cheapest discovery channel left, and the MCP package already has the most downloads (827/month).

proposals.title: docs: submit vn-skills to awesome-mcp-servers and refresh the Glama listing
proposals.body:
## Problem
The repo has 0 stars and no outside issues. The npm downloads (653–827/month) are not turning into GitHub visitors. Two MCP directories are open to us:

- **punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers**: you submit with a fork plus a PR that adds one alphabetised line (name linked to the repo, short description) in the right category. vn-skills qualifies as 📇 TypeScript, 🏠 Local. I have not confirmed whether it is already listed.
- **Glama**: searching `vn-skills` shows an entry whose description matches this project. It was last updated 2026-10-18, lists only 6 of the 11 skills (no vn-id, vn-phone, vn-holidays, vn-name, vn-number-format), and shows the licence as "Not graded". I have not confirmed that it is ours.
- **agentskills.io**: it links a Client Showcase and community channels (GitHub discussions `agentskills/agentskills`, Discord). I found no formal skill directory.

Do this after 0.5.0 is on npm, so the listed package is current.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Search awesome-mcp-servers README for `vn-skills`. If it is missing, open a PR adding one line, e.g. `[beiryu/vn-skills](https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills) 📇 🏠 - Offline Vietnam toolkit: VietQR, 34-province addresses, tax IDs, CCCD, phone, holidays, lunar calendar, money in words, e-invoices.`, under the best-fitting category
- [ ] On Glama, confirm the matching entry is beiryu/vn-skills, claim it, and update the description/tool list to all 11 skills
- [ ] Find out why Glama does not grade the MIT licence (root `LICENSE` file and `license` field in package.json) and fix what is missing
- [ ] Optional: post a short announcement in the agentskills/agentskills GitHub discussions
proposals.rationale: [needs you] These are the directories people use to compare MCP servers. A stale Glama entry with an ungraded licence ranks below competitors such as AgentPay VN.

proposals.title: vn-address: return an error instead of throwing on null or non-string input
proposals.body:
## Problem
`convertAddress(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'street')` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:58`). `searchWards(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')` because it passes the query straight to `tokenize` (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts:83-86`). `findProvince` already guards with `String(query ?? '')`, and `convertAddress('')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'EMPTY', ... } }`. The README promises "no exceptions for bad input". MCP clients that forward a missing or null field crash instead of getting `ok: false`. #95 fixed the same class of bug in vn-number-format.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Audit every exported function in `packages/core/src/address/` (`parseAddress`, `convertAddress`, `searchWards`, `findProvince`, and any other export taking a string)
- [ ] `null`, `undefined`, numbers and objects return an `ok: false` Result with a `hint` and do not throw. Use the existing `EMPTY` code for null/undefined/blank strings and the code/approach used for non-string input in `packages/core/src/numfmt` after #100 for other types
- [ ] Functions that do not return a Result handle these inputs without throwing; document the behaviour in JSDoc
- [ ] Tests in `tests/address.test.ts` cover null, undefined, a number and an object for each export
- [ ] Existing tests and golden fixtures still pass
proposals.rationale: Address conversion is the flagship skill, and MCP callers do send null fields. It also brings the module in line with the error contract fixed for numfmt.

proposals.title: vn-name: handle null and non-string input without throwing
proposals.body:
## Problem
`splitName`, `slugifyName`, `initials` and `sortNames` (`packages/core/src/name/index.ts`) call `.normalize` on their argument, directly or via `removeDiacritics`/`normalizeText` (`packages/core/src/shared/diacritics.ts:6`). Null or non-string input throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')`. Phone, taxid, CCCD, money and parseVietQR return `ok: false` for the same input.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `splitName(null | undefined | '   ')` returns the existing `EMPTY_NAME` failure. Other non-strings (numbers, objects) return an `ok: false` Result with a hint and do not throw
- [ ] `slugifyName` and `initials` (which return plain strings) return `''` for null/undefined/non-string input; documented in JSDoc
- [ ] `sortNames` does not throw when the array contains non-string entries. It drops them from the result; documented in JSDoc
- [ ] Do not change the return types (no breaking API change)
- [ ] Tests in `tests/name.test.ts` for each function with null, undefined, a number and an object
- [ ] Existing tests and golden fixtures still pass
proposals.rationale: This is the last core module that crashes on missing MCP/JSON fields, which goes against the README's 'no exceptions for bad input' promise.

proposals.title: vn-id: warn when a decoded CCCD birth year is in the future
proposals.body:
## Problem
`parseCitizenId` (`packages/core/src/id/index.ts:55-57`) computes `century = 1900 + Math.floor(digit / 2) * 100` for any digit 0–9. `parseCitizenId('001900123456')` returns `ok: true` with `birthYear: 2300` and no warning. The century coding comes from Circular 59/2021/TT-BCA, which the file already cites, so the decoding itself stays. But a birth year after the current year cannot belong to an issued card, and agents should be told.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Add an optional second argument `opts?: { today?: Date }` (default `new Date()`) so tests are deterministic
- [ ] When `birthYear` is after `today`'s year, the result keeps `ok: true` and adds a warning naming the decoded year, e.g. `Decoded birth year 2300 is in the future; the ID is probably mistyped.`
- [ ] No warning for birth years up to and including the current year
- [ ] Tests in `tests/id.test.ts` with a fixed `today`: digit 9 (future), digit 2/3 with a past year (no warning), and a birth year equal to the current year (no warning)
- [ ] CLI `id parse` and MCP `vn_id_parse` output includes the new warning (no new flags needed)
- [ ] `skills/vn-id/SKILL.md` mentions the warning
proposals.rationale: A typo in the century digit decodes silently to an impossible person. That is the kind of plausible-looking wrong answer the project exists to prevent.

proposals.title: vn-holidays: give OUT_OF_RANGE a correct hint and name the date in addWorkingDays
proposals.body:
## Problem
`checkYear` in `packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts:146-151` returns the same hint, `The data set starts with the 2023 notices.`, for years before `FIRST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` and after `LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR`. A year above 2199 gets a hint about the start of the data. Also, `addWorkingDays(30, 12, 2199, 5)` fails with only `Supported years: 2023-2199` and does not say that the walk crossed the upper bound.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Years below `FIRST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` keep the existing hint
- [ ] Years above `LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` get a hint that states the upper limit (built from the constant, e.g. `Dates after 31/12/${LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR} are not supported.`) without claiming a reason the repo does not document
- [ ] When `addWorkingDays` leaves the supported range during the walk, the message names the start date and says the result would fall outside the range
- [ ] Tests in `tests/holidays.test.ts` for a year below, a year above, and `addWorkingDays(30, 12, 2199, 5)`
- [ ] Golden case in `tests/golden/` for the year-above input → error code
proposals.rationale: The hint is wrong, which misleads agents that relay hints to users. A small, contained fix.

proposals.title: vn-phone: add hints to every error and a distinct EMPTY error
proposals.body:
## Problem
The README says every failure is `{ code, message, hint }`, but `parsePhone` (`packages/core/src/phone/index.ts`) calls `fail()` with no hint. Example: `node packages/cli/dist/index.js phone ''` prints `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_FORMAT","message":"Phone number may only contain digits, spaces, . - ( ) and a leading +"}}`. An empty input is reported as an invalid character, while address and name use an explicit EMPTY code.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Empty/whitespace/null input returns `code: 'EMPTY'` with message `Phone number is empty` and a hint
- [ ] Every other `fail(...)` in `packages/core/src/phone/` has a hint telling the user what to pass (e.g. `Use 10 digits starting with 0, or +84 followed by 9 digits.`), with no new numbering facts beyond those already in `prefixes.js`
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/phone.test.ts` that runs each error path and asserts `error.hint` is a non-empty string
- [ ] Golden case in `tests/golden/` for `''` → `EMPTY`; update existing golden cases if their codes change
- [ ] Note the new `EMPTY` code in `skills/vn-phone/SKILL.md` if it lists error codes
proposals.rationale: Agents use the hint to recover. A missing hint breaks the documented error contract on a common input.

proposals.title: cli: accept unquoted multi-word text for free-text arguments
proposals.body:
## Problem
Several commands take one free-text argument. Without quotes, the user gets a bare commander error:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js name split Tôn Thất Tùng
error: too many arguments for 'split'. Expected 1 argument but got 3: Tôn, Thất, Tùng.
```

Agents and newcomers often drop the quotes. Joining the words is unambiguous for these commands.

## Acceptance
- [ ] These commands declare a variadic argument and join the words with a single space: `name split|slug|initials` (`packages/cli/src/commands/name.ts`), `address parse|convert|wards|province` (`address.ts`), `numfmt parse` (`numfmt.ts`)
- [ ] `name sort <names...>` is unchanged (each argument is a name)
- [ ] Help text still shows one logical argument (e.g. `<fullName...>`) and says quotes are optional
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`: `name split Tôn Thất Tùng` gives the same JSON as `name split "Tôn Thất Tùng"`, and `address convert P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM` gives the same JSON as the quoted form
- [ ] README/SKILL.md examples stay quoted (no doc change required)
proposals.rationale: The first command a newcomer copies should not fail on quoting. Agents generate unquoted arguments too.

proposals.title: vietqr: do not split surrogate pairs when truncating a raw note
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:103-108`, a note with `rawNote: true` keeps its characters and is cut with `note.slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH)` (25). `slice` counts UTF-16 code units. An emoji or other astral character at position 24–25 is split, leaving a lone surrogate in the payload. That makes invalid UTF-8 when encoded or rendered to a QR image.

Out of scope: whether EMVCo/NAPAS lengths count bytes or characters (`tlvEncode` in `packages/core/src/shared/tlv.ts:15-17` uses `value.length`). The repo does not cite the spec for this; it is tracked separately and must not change here.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Truncation works on code points (e.g. `Array.from(note).slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH).join('')`), so no lone surrogate is ever produced
- [ ] Behaviour for BMP-only notes, including Vietnamese with diacritics, is unchanged (existing tests pass)
- [ ] Test in `tests/vietqr.test.ts`: 24 ASCII characters plus an emoji, with `rawNote: true`, yields a note with no lone surrogate (`/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/` does not match) and `parseVietQR` round-trips it
proposals.rationale: A corrupt payload in a payment QR is a silent failure. The surrogate fix needs no spec decision.

proposals.title: vietqr: decide whether TLV lengths count bytes or characters for non-ASCII raw notes
proposals.body:
## Problem
`tlvEncode` (`packages/core/src/shared/tlv.ts:15-17`) writes `value.length`, which counts UTF-16 code units. With `rawNote: true` a note can contain Vietnamese diacritics. Example: `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',note:'é'.repeat(30),rawNote:true})` gives a 25-character note whose UTF-8 encoding is 50 bytes. If NAPAS/EMVCo or banking apps read the length field as bytes, these payloads are misparsed. The repository does not cite which rule applies, so this needs a person with the spec.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Find the governing rule (EMVCo QRCPS-MPM and/or the NAPAS VietQR spec) and cite the section
- [ ] Optional: test a `rawNote` payload with diacritics in two or three banking apps
- [ ] Write the decision into the issue: keep character counting, switch to UTF-8 byte counting (and adjust `MAX_NOTE_LENGTH` / truncation), or forbid non-ASCII raw notes
- [ ] Then hand it to implementation with the cited source
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This could produce payment QRs that do not scan, but fixing it without the spec would mean inventing a format rule.

proposals.title: docs: state in the README that vn-skills is an offline toolkit, not a payment gateway
proposals.body:
## Problem
People comparing VietQR MCP servers on Glama also see "AgentPay VN", a Python MCP server that collects real VietQR payments. The README does not say plainly what vn-skills does and does not do for payments. It builds, parses and validates payloads offline; it does not collect money, check transfers, or call bank or NAPAS APIs. Without that line, users may expect payment confirmation, or pass vn-skills over thinking it needs credentials.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Add a short "What it is / what it is not" paragraph near the top of `README.md` (after the layer table): offline, no accounts or API keys, builds/validates VietQR payloads and images, does **not** collect payments or confirm transfers; pair it with a payment gateway for that
- [ ] The same paragraph in Vietnamese in `README.vi.md`
- [ ] One line with the same message in `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` ("Lỗi hay gặp" or an equivalent section) so agents do not promise payment confirmation
- [ ] Do not name or link competitors
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes; `pnpm format:check` passes
proposals.rationale: A clear position helps visitors from MCP directories choose vn-skills for what it does well (no credentials, works offline) instead of bouncing.

proposals.title: vietqr: collect sample MoMo, ZaloPay and VNPayQR payloads before adding parse support
proposals.body:
## Problem
`xuannghia/vietnam-qr-pay` (the upstream of `banks.json` and the top `vietqr` repo on GitHub) says it decodes VietQR, MoMo/ZaloPay multi-purpose QR and VNPayQR. `parseVietQR` handles NAPAS VietQR only. Users comparing the two will see the gap. The repository has no samples or cited spec for the wallet and VNPay formats, so they cannot be implemented without inventing format details.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Collect anonymised sample payloads for MoMo, ZaloPay and VNPayQR (or a cited public spec for each)
- [ ] Run each through `node packages/cli/dist/index.js vietqr parse <payload>` and record the current output
- [ ] Decide the scope: recognise and label the scheme only, or decode its merchant fields as well
- [ ] Add the samples (with source/licence) to the issue, then split it into implementable issues with golden fixtures
proposals.rationale: [needs you] It is the main functional gap against the most popular adjacent library, but it needs real samples that are not in the repository.

proposals.title: vietqr: say when a parsed payload was lower-cased in transit instead of reporting a bare CRC mismatch
proposals.body:
## Problem

`parseVietQR` recomputes the CRC over the payload exactly as received (`packages/core/src/vietqr/parse.ts:44-46`). When a valid payload has been lower-cased by a chat app or a form, the CRC no longer matches and the warning makes the payload look corrupted:

```
parseVietQR(buildVietQR({...}).payload.toLowerCase())
=> ok: true, crcValid: false, warnings: [
  "CRC mismatch: payload has 8300, expected E6CC.",
  "Tag 38 GUID is \"a000000727\", not NAPAS A000000727."
]
```

The CRC hex digits are already compared case-insensitively (line 46). The mismatch happens because the CRC is computed over the lower-cased payload. A scanner would compute the CRC over the payload as given too, so `crcValid: false` is the correct result. The problem is that neither warning tells the user the real cause, which is that the case was changed, not the data.

## Proposal

- When `crcValid` is false, also compute `crc16CcittFalse` over the upper-cased prefix (`payload.slice(0, crcIndex + 4).toUpperCase()`). If that matches `crc.toUpperCase()`, replace the plain CRC mismatch warning with one that says the payload appears to have been lower-cased in transit and the CRC matches the upper-cased payload. It should also tell the user to use the original payload.
- If the tag 38 GUID differs from `A000000727` only by case, warn that the GUID is lower-cased instead of saying it is not NAPAS.
- Do not change `crcValid` semantics: it stays `false` for a payload whose CRC does not match as given.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A lower-cased payload built from an upper-case-only input (for example, no note or an upper-case note) gets the new lower-case warning and no "not NAPAS" GUID warning; `crcValid` is still `false`
- [ ] A payload with a genuinely wrong CRC still gets the existing `CRC mismatch: ...` warning
- [ ] A lower-cased payload whose original had a mixed-case note (the upper-case retry does not match) keeps the plain mismatch warning and gets no false hint
- [ ] Valid payloads parse exactly as before (existing tests unchanged)
- [ ] Golden case(s) added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` in the existing case format
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: People paste payloads through tools that change case. Today the warning blames data corruption, so callers can't tell a mangled-but-recoverable code from a broken one.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: reject out-of-range day and month in parseDateInput
proposals.body:
## Problem

`parseDateInput` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:87-96`) only checks the shape of the string. `parseDateInput('0/1/2024')` returns `{ ok: true, day: 0, month: 1, year: 2024 }`, and inputs such as `32/1/2024`, `1/13/2024` and `2024-00-10` also pass. Callers re-validate later and return a generic `INVALID_DATE`, so the visible effect is a less precise error. Any caller that skips the second check would accept day 0. Non-padded forms (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`) are intentional and should stay accepted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `parseDateInput` returns `INVALID_DATE` when the month is outside 1-12 or the day is outside 1 to the number of days in that month (Gregorian, leap years included: `29/2/2024` ok, `29/2/2023` rejected)
- [ ] The error message names the bad part (e.g. `Day 0 is out of range for 01/2024`) and keeps the existing hint
- [ ] Non-padded inputs (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`, `3/2/2024`) still parse
- [ ] Tests added to `tests/lunar.test.ts` for day 0, day 32, month 0, month 13, 31/4, 29/2 in leap and non-leap years, and the non-padded forms
- [ ] Existing CLI tests (`tests/cli.test.ts`) still pass; update expected messages only where the new message is more precise
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: This is a small hardening fix. The helper is shared, so validating once here gives precise errors everywhere and removes the risk of a caller accepting day 0.

proposals.title: docs: add copy-paste MCP setup for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and Codex
proposals.body:
## Problem

`@vn-skills/mcp` is the most downloaded package (827/month), but the README's MCP section (`README.md`, "MCP server") shows only `claude mcp add` and one generic `mcpServers` JSON block. Not every client uses that shape. VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json` uses a top-level `servers` key, and Codex reads TOML from `~/.codex/config.toml`. A user who pastes the generic JSON into one of those clients gets a server that never starts, and the README doesn't say where each file goes. `docs/quickstart.md` has the same gap.

This is the install-guide half of RM-003. The demo GIF half is tracked in #92.

## Proposal

Add a short "MCP client setup" subsection to `README.md` (and the same in `README.vi.md`) with one block per client:

- **Claude Code:** keep `claude mcp add vn-skills -- npx -y @vn-skills/mcp`
- **Claude Desktop:** `claude_desktop_config.json`, `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Cursor:** `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global), same `mcpServers` shape
- **VS Code:** `.vscode/mcp.json`, `{ "servers": { "vn-skills": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Codex:** `~/.codex/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  [mcp_servers.vn-skills]
  command = "npx"
  args = ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"]
  ```

Link each client to its official MCP documentation page so readers can check the file location. Keep the generic block for other clients. Mention that Node.js 22+ is required.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `README.md` has a block for each of the five clients above, each with a link to that client's MCP docs
- [ ] `README.vi.md` has the same content in Vietnamese
- [ ] `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` link to the new section instead of duplicating it
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes (extend it if it checks the MCP section)
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` passes
proposals.rationale: MCP is the channel with the most downloads, and getting set up in a client is the step where people drop off. Snippets that work as pasted for each client turn downloads into working installs.

proposals.title: docs: get vn-skills listed on the skills.sh leaderboard
proposals.body:
## Problem

skills.sh shows an Agent Skills leaderboard with install counts and 8-week activity per source repo (for example `microsoft/azure-skills`). `https://skills.sh/beiryu/vn-skills` returned 404 on 2026-10-23, so vn-skills is not listed. How repos get onto the leaderboard has not been confirmed: it could be a submission form, a docs page, or installs going through their tooling. This directory is separate from agentskills.io and the MCP directories in #109.

## Checklist

- [ ] Read the skills.sh docs or about page and record how a repo gets listed (submission, automatic indexing, or install telemetry)
- [ ] If there is a submission path, submit `beiryu/vn-skills` (11 skills under `skills/`, MIT)
- [ ] If listing depends on a specific install command, open a follow-up issue to add that command to `README.md`, `README.vi.md` and `docs/quickstart.md` next to `npx -y @vn-skills/cli install`
- [ ] Confirm `https://skills.sh/beiryu/vn-skills` resolves and note the date here
proposals.rationale: [needs you] The repo has 0 stars, and npm downloads aren't bringing visitors to GitHub. A leaderboard that ranks skill repos by installs is a discovery channel aimed straight at the Agent Skills users we want.

proposals.title: vn-einvoice: check whether Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP changes the rules or citations
proposals.body:
## Problem

`skills/vn-einvoice/SKILL.md`, `skills/vn-einvoice/references/schema.md`, `packages/core/src/einvoice/schema.ts` and the `vn_einvoice_validate` MCP tool description cite only Decree 123/2020/NĐ-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Published pages refer to a Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP that amends Decree 123/2020 on invoices and documents. Its text could not be read online: thuvienphapluat.vn returned 403 and the chinhphu.vn URL returned 404. Nothing in the repository says what it changes, so no code can change until the governing text is checked.

## Checklist

- [ ] Get the official text of Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP (official gazette or chinhphu.vn) and record the URL and effective date in this issue
- [ ] Decide whether it changes anything the schema validates: required fields, invoice symbol or number format, buyer and seller fields, VAT handling or amount-in-words
- [ ] If nothing changes: open a follow-up to add the decree to the citations in `SKILL.md`, `references/schema.md`, `schema.ts` and the MCP description
- [ ] If rules change: open one follow-up issue per rule, each quoting the article and the expected input → output, so the change can be made with golden tests in `tests/golden/vn-einvoice.json`
proposals.rationale: [needs you] An e-invoice skill that cites outdated law loses trust fast. The legal reading needs a person, and the code work stays blocked until then.

proposals.title: vn-tax-id: return a distinct EMPTY error for empty or blank input
proposals.body:
## Problem

`validateTaxId` (`packages/core/src/taxid/index.ts`) reports an empty or whitespace-only input as `INVALID_FORMAT` with the message `contains non-digit characters`, which is wrong: there are no characters at all. `normalizeTaxId` returns `null` for `''`, and `validateTaxId` maps every `null` to the non-digit message (lines ~66-73).

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json taxid validate ""
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_FORMAT","message":"Tax ID \"\" contains non-digit characters","hint":"Only digits, spaces, dots and dashes are accepted."}}
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json taxid validate "   "
(same INVALID_FORMAT / non-digit message)
```

Since #123, `vn-phone` returns a distinct `EMPTY` code with a hint for empty input, and `vn-address` returns `EMPTY` for `''`. Tax ID should behave the same way.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `validateTaxId('')`, `validateTaxId('   ')`, `validateTaxId(null as any)` and `validateTaxId(undefined as any)` return `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'EMPTY', message, hint } }`, and the message does not mention non-digit characters
- [ ] The hint says which forms are accepted. Reuse the wording already in the `validateTaxId` doc comment: 10 digits, 13 digits / `10-3` with a dash, or a 12-digit personal ID
- [ ] Non-empty inputs with letters (e.g. `abc`) still return `INVALID_FORMAT` as today
- [ ] Golden cases for `''` and `'   '` in the vn-tax-id fixture under `tests/golden/`, if that fixture format supports error cases; otherwise unit tests in `tests/taxid.test.ts`
- [ ] A CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`: `taxid validate ""` prints `code: "EMPTY"`
- [ ] If `skills/vn-tax-id/SKILL.md` lists error codes, add `EMPTY`
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: Error messages for empty input are now consistent across phone and address. Tax ID is the remaining outlier, and its message points the user at the wrong problem.

proposals.title: vietqr: handle null and non-string notes in sanitizeNote and buildVietQR without throwing
proposals.body:
## Problem

`sanitizeNote` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:40`) is exported from `@vn-skills/core` and passes its argument straight to `removeDiacritics`, which calls `.normalize`. A `null` note throws:

```
sanitizeNote(null) -> TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')
```

`buildVietQR` has the same issue one level up. Around line 101 it checks `opts.note !== undefined && opts.note.trim() !== ''`, so `buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', note: null })` also throws (`null.trim`). A numeric note (`note: 123`) throws too. MCP and library callers that forward JSON with `"note": null` crash instead of getting a Result. #110 (address) and #111 (name) fixed the same class of bug in other modules but not here.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `sanitizeNote(null)` and `sanitizeNote(undefined)` return `''`; `sanitizeNote(123 as any)` returns `'123'` (coerce with `String(x ?? '')`)
- [ ] `buildVietQR` treats `note: null` like an omitted note (no tag 08 / no note, `ok: true`)
- [ ] `buildVietQR` with a non-string note (e.g. `123`) coerces it to a string and sanitises it as usual, also with `rawNote: true`
- [ ] Existing note behaviour (sanitising, truncation to the max length by code point, warnings) is unchanged; existing vietqr tests pass
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` for all of the above
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: VietQR is the main skill. A JSON null note from an MCP client should not crash the call when every other module now returns ok:false or ignores the value.

proposals.title: vn-einvoice: report an error instead of a blank amount in words when totals are not finite or too large
proposals.body:
## Problem

`computeTotals` (`packages/core/src/einvoice/totals.ts:37-80`) multiplies `quantity * unitPrice` with no checks and ends with `totalInWords: words.ok ? words.words : ''`. That hides two failures:

- A non-numeric quantity (library callers that skip `validateInvoice`) makes `grandTotal` `NaN` (shown as `null` in JSON).
- Values that pass `validateInvoice` but overflow (e.g. `quantity: 1e300, unitPrice: 1e300`; `isNum` in `schema.ts:73` only checks `Number.isFinite` on each field) give an `Infinity` total, `moneyToWords` fails and `totalInWords` is `''`.

In both cases there is no error. The CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts:57`), the MCP tool `vn_einvoice_totals` (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:534`) and the mock adapter (`packages/core/src/einvoice/adapters/mock.ts:45`) return `ok: true` with a blank "Số tiền bằng chữ".

## Acceptance

- [ ] `validateInvoice` adds an error at `lines[i]` when `quantity * unitPrice` is not finite or its absolute value exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (a JavaScript precision limit, not a legal threshold)
- [ ] `InvoiceTotals` gets an optional `totalInWordsError?: VnError` field. `computeTotals` sets it when any total is not finite or `moneyToWords` returns `ok: false` (passing on that error), and `totalInWords` stays `''` in that case. The current signature and fields are otherwise unchanged
- [ ] `vn-skills einvoice totals` and the `vn_einvoice_totals` MCP tool return `{ ok: false, error }` when `totalInWordsError` is set
- [ ] `mockIssue` does not issue a mock invoice with a blank amount in words; it returns `ok: false` with that error
- [ ] Tests in `tests/einvoice.test.ts` (non-numeric quantity passed directly to `computeTotals`, the 1e300 case through `validateInvoice`, the CLI and MCP paths), plus a case in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] The normal example (`vn-skills einvoice example | vn-skills einvoice totals`) output is unchanged
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: A blank amount in words reported as success is the kind of silent wrong output that makes people stop trusting the e-invoice skill.

proposals.title: mcp: make the MCP Registry description cover all 11 skills
proposals.body:
## Problem

vn-skills is live in the official MCP Registry (`io.github.beiryu/vn-skills`, 0.6.0, active). Its description comes from `packages/mcp/server.json`:

> Vietnam tools: VietQR, addresses, tax IDs, CCCD, holidays, money in words, lunar calendar, e-invoice

It leaves out phone numbers, names and number formatting, and does not say the server is offline. Aggregators that import the registry show this text as-is. The registry rejects descriptions longer than 100 characters.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `packages/mcp/server.json` `description` is at most 100 characters and mentions phone numbers, names and number/date formatting along with the existing areas. Shorter wording such as "tax ID", "CCCD" or "lunar" is fine to make it fit; mention "offline" if it still fits
- [ ] `packages/mcp/package.json` `description` (if shorter or different) stays consistent
- [ ] A test in `tests/package-metadata.test.ts` asserts `server.json` `description.length <= 100` and that `server.json` `version` and `packages[0].version` equal `packages/mcp/package.json` `version`
- [ ] No change to `.github/workflows/` or release config. The registry picks up the new text on the next release through the existing publish job
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The registry entry is now live and feeds other directories. With 0 stars and about 800 MCP downloads a month, its one line of text is the main way people find the server, and it leaves out 3 of the 11 skills.

proposals.title: docs: group the MCP tool list by skill in README.md and README.vi.md
proposals.body:
## Problem

The README "MCP server" section lists 28 tools as one comma-separated line (`vietqr_build`, `vietqr_parse`, …, `vn_holidays_add_working_days`) in no particular order. For example, `vn_tax_id_check_digit` sits between lunar tools. A reader can't quickly see what each skill exposes. Comparable offline MCP servers in directories (e.g. `josemvelez/mcp-latam-business` on Smithery) group tools by module and give a count.

## Acceptance

- [ ] In `README.md`, replace the flat `Tools:` line with a short table or list grouped by skill (vietqr, vn-address, vn-tax-id, vn-id, vn-phone, vn-holidays, vn-money-words, vn-lunar, vn-einvoice, vn-name, vn-number-format), with the total tool count in the heading or first sentence
- [ ] The tool names and count are taken from `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` (every registered tool listed exactly once, none invented)
- [ ] Same change in `README.vi.md`, with Vietnamese prose
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes. If it checks the tool list, keep that check (or extend it so it fails when a tool registered in `server.ts` is missing from the README)
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm exec vitest run` pass
proposals.rationale: The README is the landing page for npm and directory visitors. A grouped tool list shows the breadth of the server at a glance, which is the main argument for adopting it.

proposals.title: mcp: add an MCPB manifest and a script that packs @vn-skills/mcp into a .mcpb bundle
proposals.body:
## Problem

There is no MCPB bundle (formerly DXT) for the MCP server. The repo has no MCPB/DXT manifest; the only match for those words is in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. MCPB is a zip holding the server plus a `manifest.json`. Claude Desktop (macOS/Windows) installs it with a single click, and it is the only way to publish a stdio, offline server on Smithery (URL publishing needs a hosted HTTP server). Smithery searches for `vietnam` and `vn-skills` return no Vietnam server.

Format reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/mcpb/main/README.md (the CLI is `@anthropic-ai/mcpb`: `mcpb init`, `mcpb validate`, `mcpb pack`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `packages/mcp/manifest.json` follows the current MCPB manifest spec (use the `manifest_version` the mcpb README documents; check it with `mcpb validate`): name `vn-skills`, version equal to `packages/mcp/package.json`, description/author/repository/license (MIT) taken from the existing package metadata, a Node server entry pointing at the built `dist/index.js`, and a `tools` list with the name and short description of every tool registered in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`
- [ ] `@anthropic-ai/mcpb` added as a devDependency and a `bundle` script in `packages/mcp/package.json` that builds and runs `mcpb pack`, writing `vn-skills.mcpb`. The bundle must include the server's runtime dependencies, including `@vn-skills/core` and its `data/*.json`. Note the bundle size in the PR
- [ ] Generated `.mcpb` files are git-ignored and not included in the npm package (`files` in `packages/mcp/package.json` unchanged or explicitly excluding them)
- [ ] A test (e.g. in `tests/package-metadata.test.ts` or `tests/mcp.test.ts`) asserts the manifest version equals the package version and the manifest tool names equal the tools registered by `createServer()`
- [ ] If release-please updates versions in `server.json`, check whether `manifest.json` needs the same treatment and say so in the PR; do not edit release config or `.github/workflows/` in this issue
- [ ] A short "Claude Desktop (MCPB)" note in the README MCP client setup section and in `README.vi.md`, saying how to build the bundle locally until it ships with releases
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: MCP downloads (827/month) lead the three packages, and Smithery has no Vietnam server. A bundle unlocks one-click Claude Desktop install and a Smithery listing for non-developers who won't edit JSON config.

proposals.title: mcp: ship the .mcpb bundle with each release and publish it on Smithery
proposals.body:
## Problem

Once the MCPB manifest and `bundle` script exist (see the issue "mcp: add an MCPB manifest and a script that packs @vn-skills/mcp into a .mcpb bundle"), the bundle still has to be distributed. That needs release-config changes and a Smithery account, so a maintainer has to do it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Wait until the MCPB manifest/bundle issue is merged and released
- [ ] Decide whether to attach `vn-skills.mcpb` to each GitHub Release. If yes, add a step to the release workflow after the npm publish (build, `pnpm --filter @vn-skills/mcp bundle`, upload the asset)
- [ ] Install the bundle in Claude Desktop on macOS or Windows and check that `vietqr_build` and `vn_address_convert` work offline
- [ ] Publish on Smithery as a local server: `smithery mcp publish ./vn-skills.mcpb -n beiryu/vn-skills` (or the web flow), following https://smithery.ai/docs/build/publish
- [ ] Use the same short description as `packages/mcp/server.json` and mark the server offline / no auth
- [ ] Check https://smithery.ai/servers?q=vietnam lists it, then add the Smithery link to the README MCP section (and `README.vi.md`)
- [ ] Consider submitting the bundle to the Claude Desktop extensions directory, if a submission path is open
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This is the distribution step that makes the bundle matter: Smithery has no Vietnam server today. It needs an account and release-workflow changes, so a person does it.

proposals.title: python: split RM-020 (PyPI port) into shippable slices
proposals.body:
## Problem

The README says a Python port is "next up", and ROADMAP RM-020 describes a `vn-skills` package on PyPI that passes the shared `tests/golden/*.json` fixtures. RM-020 is `size: l`, and ROADMAP rules say `size: l` items must be split before work starts. A competing VietQR MCP server is already on PyPI (AgentPay VN, seen on Glama), so Python users currently have no offline vn-skills option. No slice is defined yet, so nothing can be built.

## Checklist (maintainer decisions)

- [ ] Check the PyPI name `vn-skills` is available and reserve it (or choose another name)
- [ ] Decide the layout (`python/` at the repo root vs `packages/python`), the minimum Python version and the build tool
- [ ] Decide how bundled data reaches Python (copy `packages/core/data/*.json` at build time vs a shared data package), without breaking the rule that the JSON is only produced by `scripts/build-data.ts`
- [ ] Decide the CI job (a Python test run against `tests/golden/`) and whether release-please manages the Python version
- [ ] Choose the order of skills. A pure-logic first slice whose golden fixtures already exist (e.g. money-to-words, then tax ID, then VietQR) keeps the first PR at `size: s`/`m`
- [ ] File one `[RM-020]` issue per slice with acceptance "passes `tests/golden/<skill>.json`", and update ROADMAP.md
proposals.rationale: [needs you] The README advertises the Python port as next, but it is blocked on decisions only the maintainer can make. Splitting it unblocks small, testable slices.

proposals.title: repo: pin the plugin's MCP server to an exact version and give plugin.json a version
proposals.body:
## Problem
The Claude Code plugin (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with `source: "./"`) is not ready for Anthropic's plugin directory:

1. `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp` with no version. The pre-submission checklist (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/pre-submission-checklist.md) treats an "Unpinned npx launcher" as **Blocks**: every package a launcher runs must be pinned to an exact version.
2. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` has no `version`. The checklist warns about this, and the docs say to raise it on every release.

`tests/plugin.test.ts` currently enforces both problems: `plugin.json has metadata and no version` asserts `not.toHaveProperty('version')`, and `.mcp.json runs npx -y @vn-skills/mcp` asserts `args` equals `['-y', '@vn-skills/mcp']`.

The pinned version must follow the release version in `packages/mcp/package.json`, which release-please bumps (see `release-please-config.json` `extra-files`). The release-please `json` updater can update `plugin.json`'s `$.version`. It cannot update `.mcp.json`, because the version sits inside the string `@vn-skills/mcp@X.Y.Z`, and JSON cannot hold the `x-release-please-version` marker the generic updater needs.

This issue explicitly covers editing `release-please-config.json`. Do not touch `.github/workflows/`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.mcp.json` args are `["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp@<version>"]`, where `<version>` equals `version` in `packages/mcp/package.json`.
- [ ] `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` has `"version"` equal to `packages/mcp/package.json` `version`.
- [ ] `release-please-config.json` `extra-files` gains `{ "type": "json", "path": ".claude-plugin/plugin.json", "jsonpath": "$.version" }`.
- [ ] A script `scripts/sync-plugin-version.ts` (exposed as `pnpm sync-plugin-version`) rewrites the `.mcp.json` pin from `packages/mcp/package.json`. Running it twice changes nothing.
- [ ] `tests/plugin.test.ts`: replace the two assertions above with tests that (a) `plugin.json` `version` equals the MCP package version and (b) `.mcp.json` args equal `['-y', '@vn-skills/mcp@' + version]`. A release PR that forgets the sync then fails CI with a message that names `pnpm sync-plugin-version`.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md (release section) says: on the release PR, run `pnpm sync-plugin-version` and push the change.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: With 0 stars, the Claude plugin directory (shown in Claude Code under /plugin > Discover) is a channel that could put vn-skills in front of Claude Code users. The unpinned npx launcher alone would get the submission rejected.

proposals.title: docs: submit the vn-skills plugin to Anthropic's plugin directory
proposals.body:
## Problem
Anthropic's plugin directory (claude.ai/directory, also shown in Claude Code under `/plugin` > Discover) takes plugin bundles from public GitHub repos through the developer portal at claude.ai/directory/manage. Submitting needs a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan. The first organization to submit a repo folder owns the listing. vn-skills already ships a plugin at the repo root (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json` with `source: "./"`), but it is not listed.

The directory also no longer accepts MCPB desktop extensions: "the directory no longer accepts local MCP servers packaged as desktop extensions (MCPB). To distribute a local MCP server through the directory, include it in a plugin bundle" (https://claude.com/docs/directory/publish). For Claude, the plugin is therefore the route, and #146 (MCPB bundle, p1) matters mainly for Smithery (#147).

This needs the maintainer's account and plan.

## Checklist
- [ ] Wait until the issue "repo: pin the plugin's MCP server to an exact version and give plugin.json a version" is merged and released.
- [ ] Run `claude plugin validate .` at the repo root and fix any errors.
- [ ] Check the review triggers in https://claude.com/docs/plugins/pre-submission-checklist.md: non-image files over 256 KiB (for example `packages/core/data/*.json`) and more than 512 files in the plugin folder (the whole repo root). Either one sends the plugin to manual review but does not block it. Decide whether to accept that or to move the plugin into a subfolder.
- [ ] Submit the repo at claude.ai/directory/manage under the beiryu organization.
- [ ] Lower #146 to `priority: p2`, and edit its Problem text to drop the Claude-directory motivation.
- [ ] Once listed, add the directory link to README.md and README.vi.md.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This listing is a discovery channel inside Claude Code itself. Traction is at 0 stars and about 800 MCP downloads a month, and the first submitter owns the listing.

proposals.title: vn-address: convert a file or stdin of addresses in one command (lines or a CSV column)
proposals.body:
## Problem
The main job for the 63→34 province change is migrating stored customer addresses in bulk. `vn-skills address convert <text...>` (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts`) converts one address per process. The only file/stdin input in the CLI is `einvoice` (`packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts:16`, `file === '-' ? readFileSync(0, 'utf8') : ...`), and `packages/core/src/address` has no batch path. Competing npm packages advertise bulk conversion. For example, `vietnam-address-kit` describes itself as offering "search, validation, normalization, conversion, and CSV migration" (npm search, 2026-10-23: https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=vietnam%20address%2034%20provinces&size=6).

This reuses the existing mapping data and `convertAddress`; it needs no new data.

## Proposal
Add a subcommand `vn-skills address convert-file <file>`, where `-` means stdin.
- Default input is one address per line; blank lines are skipped. Output is one JSON object per line (NDJSON), with the same fields as `address convert` plus `line` (1-based). Failed lines give `{ ok: false, line, input, error }` and do not stop the run.
- `--csv --column <name>`: input is CSV with a header row (RFC 4180 quoting, including commas and newlines inside quoted fields). Output is CSV with all original columns plus `new_address`, `new_ward_code`, `new_province_code`, `mapping_type`, `confidence`, `warnings` (joined with `; `). Write a small parser in `packages/cli/src`; do not add a dependency.
- Exit code 0 when every row converted. Exit code 2 when some rows failed, with a one-line summary on stderr (`converted N, failed M`).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `address convert-file` exists and is listed in `vn-skills address --help`.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` use temp files: a 3-line file (one old address from the README, `P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM`, one blank line, one empty/garbage line), stdin via `-`, a CSV with a quoted field containing a comma, a missing `--column` name (clear error), and the exit code 2 case.
- [ ] The `line` numbers and the CSV column order are asserted.
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` documents the command with a Vietnamese trigger phrase (e.g. "chuyển hàng loạt địa chỉ", "file CSV"); `tests/golden/triggers.json` still passes.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md show one example.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Bulk migration of customer databases is the most common reason people look for 34-province tooling, and the npm competitors (about 1–12k downloads/month) already offer it. This closes the gap with existing data.

proposals.title: cli: accept negative amounts in `money words` or explain how to pass them
proposals.body:
## Problem
Commander reads a negative amount as an option:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json money words -5
error: unknown option '-5'
```

The command does handle negative amounts: `money words -- -5` gives `{"ok": true, "amount": "-5", "words": "âm năm đồng"}`. But neither the error nor `money words --help` mentions `--`. See `packages/cli/src/commands/money.ts`; the `words <amount>` command defines short options `-u` and `-c`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `vn-skills money words -5` prints `âm năm đồng` (exit 0). If supporting this cleanly in commander is not possible, the command instead fails with a message that tells the user to run `vn-skills money words -- -5`.
- [ ] Negative amounts work together with options, e.g. `money words -1200000 --thousand ngàn`, or the same hint is shown.
- [ ] `-u`/`-c` and other existing options keep working. A real unknown option such as `--foo` still errors.
- [ ] `money words --help` shows how to pass a negative amount.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` cover `-5`, `-- -5`, a negative amount with an option, and `--foo`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: A newcomer tried this and got a bare 'unknown option' error with no way forward. A small fix removes that first-run confusion.

proposals.title: vn-phone: accept +84 followed by the trunk 0 (e.g. '+84 0912345678')
proposals.body:
## Problem
`parsePhone` (`packages/core/src/phone/index.ts:57`) runs `if (digits.startsWith('84')) digits = '0' + digits.slice(2);`. With input `+84 0912345678` or `84-0912345678`, that gives `00912345678` (11 digits). The number is then read as a landline, and the error names digits the user never typed:

```
parsePhone('+84 0912345678')
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNKNOWN_PREFIX","message":"Unknown area code or prefix 0091","hint":"Check the area code or prefix at the start of the number."}}
```

Writing the country code and keeping the trunk `0` is a common mistake. A national significant number after a country code never starts with the trunk prefix, so dropping that one `0` is safe. This matches how the function already silently converts old 11-digit mobile numbers (`convertedFrom`).

## Acceptance
- [ ] When the input starts with `84` or `+84` and the next digit is `0`, drop that `0` before the rest of the parsing. Apply this only to input that started with the country code; input starting with `0` keeps its current behaviour.
- [ ] `parsePhone('+84 0912345678')` and `parsePhone('84-0912345678')` return ok with `national: '0912345678'` and `e164: '+84912345678'`, the same carrier as `0912345678`, and a note that the extra 0 was removed. Add an optional `warnings` (or similar) field to `PhoneInfo` and expose it in the CLI/MCP output, the same way other fields are exposed.
- [ ] A landline written the same way (`+84 0` + a valid number from the existing fixtures) parses like its national form.
- [ ] Golden cases added to the phone fixture under `tests/golden/` that `tests/phone-golden.test.ts` loads, covering both mobile forms and one landline form. Existing cases still pass.
- [ ] `skills/vn-phone/SKILL.md` mentions the case in its pitfalls section, if it has one.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Agents fed real user input will hit this. The current error is misleading, and the fix needs no new Vietnamese data.

proposals.title: vn-money-words: cap the digit count so a long amount string cannot exhaust memory
proposals.body:
## Problem

`moneyToWords` in `packages/core/src/money/index.ts` accepts a digit string (or bigint) of any length and converts it with `BigInt(cleaned)`. Output grows quadratically with input length: `scaleWord(i, thousand)` appends `'tỷ'` `Math.floor(i / 3)` times for group `i`, and every non-zero group gets its own scale word.

Measured with `moneyToWords('9'.repeat(n))`:

- `n = 20000` → ok, a 22,407,778-character string, ~270 ms
- `n = 200000` → `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`. The process aborts, and `try/catch` cannot recover.

Every caller that forwards user text reaches this path:

- `vn-skills money words <amount>` (`packages/cli/src/commands/money.ts`)
- the `vn_money_to_words` MCP tool (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`)
- `numberToWords`
- e-invoice totals in words

One oversized argument can kill a long-running MCP server.

## Fix

Add an exported constant (for example `MAX_MONEY_DIGITS`; 1000 is a reasonable value, and the output stays well under 100 KB) and check it before any heavy work:

- **String input:** after removing separators and the sign, and **before** `BigInt(cleaned)`, return `fail('INVALID_AMOUNT', ...)` when the digit count exceeds the limit. Give a hint that names the limit.
- **bigint input:** check `(big < 0n ? -big : big).toString().length` the same way.
- **number input:** already capped by `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. No change.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `moneyToWords('9'.repeat(MAX_MONEY_DIGITS))` returns `ok: true`.
- [ ] `moneyToWords('9'.repeat(MAX_MONEY_DIGITS + 1))` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_AMOUNT', hint } }` and finishes in well under a second.
- [ ] `moneyToWords('9'.repeat(200000))` returns the same error instead of crashing the test process.
- [ ] The bigint path is covered: `10n ** BigInt(MAX_MONEY_DIGITS)` is rejected.
- [ ] A negative string over the limit is rejected; the `-` sign does not count as a digit.
- [ ] `numberToWords` gets the same limit (it delegates to `moneyToWords`).
- [ ] Add a golden case to `tests/golden/vn-money-words.json` if the fixture format supports error cases; otherwise add the tests to `tests/money.test.ts`.
- [ ] `skills/vn-money-words/SKILL.md` states the maximum digit count.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: An unbounded input crashes the MCP server and CLI with an unrecoverable out-of-memory error. It is a one-line guard plus tests, and it protects the long-running MCP server, which is the most-downloaded package.

proposals.title: cli: add `install --agent agents` to copy skills into .agents/skills
proposals.body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts` knows three targets:

```ts
const AGENT_DIRS = { claude: '.claude', cursor: '.cursor', codex: '.codex' };
```

The current skills docs from three agents all list `.agents/skills` (project) and `~/.agents/skills` (user) as a discovery location:

- **Codex** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills, redirected from https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills) lists `$CWD/.agents/skills`, `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills` and `$HOME/.agents/skills`. It does not list `.codex/skills`.
- **Cursor** (https://cursor.com/docs/skills) lists `.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/` as main locations and reads `.codex/skills` only for compatibility.
- **Gemini CLI** (https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) also reads `.agents/skills`.

There is no way to install into that shared folder today. `README.md`, `README.vi.md`, `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` only mention `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.codex`.

This issue adds the new target only. Whether `--agent codex` should move to `.agents/skills` is a separate decision that needs a check against a current Codex CLI, so leave the `codex` mapping unchanged.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `AGENT_DIRS` gains `agents: '.agents'`. `vn-skills install <skill|all> --agent agents` writes to `./.agents/skills/<name>`, or to `~/.agents/skills/<name>` with `--global`.
- [ ] The `--agent` help text and the unknown-agent error list `agents`.
- [ ] `--force` and `--dry-run` behave as they do for the other agents.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`, using a temp dir like the existing install tests: project scope, `--dry-run` output, and the refusal to overwrite without `--force`.
- [ ] `README.md` and `README.vi.md`:
  - The `--agent` list includes `agents`.
  - The "Cursor / Codex / other agents" paragraph says `.agents/skills/` is read by Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, citing the docs above.
- [ ] `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` get the same update.
- [ ] Do not edit `ROADMAP.md`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Codex users who follow the README may install skills into a folder Codex no longer scans, so their first try fails silently. One shared target covers Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI at once, which helps adoption beyond Claude Code.

proposals.title: cli: check whether current Codex still loads .codex/skills and decide what `--agent codex` targets
proposals.body:
## Problem

`vn-skills install --agent codex` copies skills into `.codex/skills` (`packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts`). `README.md`, `README.vi.md`, `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` tell Codex users to use that folder.

OpenAI's current skills page (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) lists these discovery locations:

- `$CWD/.agents/skills`, parent folders, `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills`
- `$HOME/.agents/skills`
- `/etc/codex/skills`
- bundled skills

It does not list `.codex/skills`. Whether Codex still reads `.codex/skills` as a legacy path could not be confirmed from the docs. Only a run against a current Codex CLI can settle it.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] With the latest Codex CLI, run `npx -y @vn-skills/cli install vietqr --agent codex` in a scratch project. Then ask Codex something that should trigger the skill (e.g. "tạo QR chuyển 500k vào VCB số tài khoản 0011001234567"). Record whether the skill loads.
- [ ] Repeat with `~/.codex/skills` (`--global`).
- [ ] Decide:
  - (a) keep `codex → .codex`,
  - (b) point `codex` at `.agents`, or
  - (c) keep it and print a note recommending `--agent agents`.
- [ ] If (b) or (c), open a follow-up issue with exact acceptance criteria, including README/quickstart updates in both languages.
- [ ] Optional: OpenAI says reusable skills should ship as plugins in a plugin directory shared by ChatGPT and Codex. Check how to submit one, and file a separate issue if it is open to third parties.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] The README's Codex instructions may point at a folder Codex ignores. Changing the default without a hands-on check could break users for whom it works today.

proposals.title: repo: add a gemini-extension.json so Gemini CLI installs all skills plus the MCP server
proposals.body:
## Problem

Gemini CLI installs extensions straight from a GitHub repo (`gemini extensions install https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills`). Its gallery at geminicli.com/extensions finds tagged public repos on its own, checking daily (https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/releasing/). The repo has no `gemini-extension.json` at its root, so neither path works today.

An extension can bundle Agent Skills from a root `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` folder (https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/), which matches our layout. It can also declare `mcpServers` (https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/reference/). A gallery search for "vietnam" returns only general-purpose extensions.

This issue is explicitly about release config: the manifest's version has to follow each release, the same way `packages/mcp/server.json` does.

## Work

1. Add `gemini-extension.json` at the repo root, following the reference docs above.
   - `name`: `vn-skills`
   - `version`: the current `packages/mcp/package.json` version
   - `description`: the npm description of the CLI or MCP package, or a shortened version of it
   - `mcpServers.vn-skills`: `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp@<same version>"] }`
   - Use only fields documented in the reference.
2. Add two `extra-files` entries to `release-please-config.json` so release-please bumps the manifest's `$.version` and the pinned version inside the `args` string. If a JSONPath entry cannot rewrite part of a string, use a `generic` file with an `x-release-please-version` marker. Release Please's `generic` updater rewrites a marked line, so it does not work on a JSON file. Instead, add a vitest check that fails when the two versions differ.
3. Add a test, in `tests/plugin.test.ts` or a new `tests/gemini-extension.test.ts`, that:
   - parses `gemini-extension.json`
   - checks `name`, `version` and `description` are present
   - checks `version` equals `packages/mcp/package.json` `version`
   - checks the `args` pin `@vn-skills/mcp@<that version>`
4. README.md and README.vi.md: add a **Gemini CLI** line to "Install the skills" with `gemini extensions install https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `gemini-extension.json` exists at the root, ends with a newline, and passes the test above.
- [ ] `release-please-config.json` keeps its version in step with releases (or the test guards it, as above).
- [ ] Both READMEs document the install command.
- [ ] Do not change `.github/workflows/`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.

The repo topic `gemini-cli-extension` that the gallery also needs is a separate, maintainer-only step.
proposals.rationale: With 0 stars and ~700–850 npm downloads a month, the project needs discovery channels where its niche is empty. The Gemini gallery lists repos without any submission and has no Vietnam extension, and one manifest exposes all 11 skills and 28 tools.

proposals.title: docs: add the gemini-cli-extension topic so vn-skills appears in the Gemini CLI extension gallery
proposals.body:
## Problem

The Gemini CLI extension gallery (geminicli.com/extensions) finds public repos that have the GitHub topic `gemini-cli-extension` and a root `gemini-extension.json` (https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/releasing/). On 2026-10-24 the repo topics were `agent-skills, claude-code, mcp, typescript, vietnam, vietqr` (https://api.github.com/repos/beiryu/vn-skills/topics). Only the repo owner can change topics.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Add the repo topic `gemini-cli-extension` (repo settings → About → Topics).
