proposals.title: vn-tax-id: treat '_' like a dash so a mistyped branch ID is not accepted as a 12-digit personal ID
proposals.body:
## Problem

`normalizeTaxId` (`packages/core/src/taxid/index.ts:50`) strips `_` along with spaces, dots and dashes:

```ts
.replace(/[\s.\-–_]/g, '')
```

The branch check in `validateTaxId` (`packages/core/src/taxid/index.ts:84`) only recognises `-` and `–` as the root/branch separator:

```ts
const dashed = /^\s*(\d[\d\s.]*)[-–]\s*(\d+)\s*$/.exec(String(input ?? ''));
```

That check exists so that `0100233488-01` is not mistaken for a 12-digit personal ID. With an underscore it never runs:

```text
validateTaxId('0100233488_01')
→ {"ok":true,"normalized":"010023348801","kind":"personal-id","checksumValid":null,...}

validateTaxId('0100233488-01')
→ {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_LENGTH","message":"Branch tax IDs must be 10 digits, a dash, then 3 digits (got 10-2)"}}
```

So a truncated branch ID passes as a valid CCCD tax ID and its check digit is never checked. Also, the docstring ("Strip spaces, dots and dashes") and the INVALID_FORMAT hint ("Only digits, spaces, dots and dashes are accepted.") don't mention `_`, even though it is accepted.

## Fix

Keep accepting `_` so `0100233488_001` stays valid. Treat it as a root/branch separator, exactly like `-` and `–`: add `_` to the character class in the `dashed` regex. Then update the `normalizeTaxId` docstring and the INVALID_FORMAT hint to list underscores as an accepted separator.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `validateTaxId('0100233488_01')` returns `ok:false` with code `INVALID_LENGTH` and the same `10-2` message as the dash form
- [ ] `validateTaxId('0100233488_001')` still returns `ok:true` with `kind: 'branch'` and `formatted: '0100233488-001'`
- [ ] Golden cases for both inputs added to `tests/golden/vn-tax-id.json`, using the existing fixture shape
- [ ] The `normalizeTaxId` docstring and the INVALID_FORMAT hint mention underscores
- [ ] If `skills/vn-tax-id/SKILL.md` or its references list the accepted separators, they mention `_` too
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: A wrong ok:true from a validator is worse than an error: callers store a truncated branch ID as a valid personal tax ID. The fix is one regex plus golden cases.

proposals.title: vn-number-format: round the decimal the user wrote, so formatNumber(2.675) gives 2,68
proposals.body:
## Problem

`formatNumber` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts:25`) rounds with `abs.toFixed(digits)`. `toFixed` rounds the binary double, not the decimal the caller wrote. 2.675 is stored as 2.67499999…, so:

```text
formatNumber(2.675, { maxFractionDigits: 2 }) → { ok: true, text: '2,67' }
```

People reading a money-like display expect `2,68`. This affects the CLI `numfmt format` path (`packages/cli/src/commands/numfmt.ts:22`), the `vn_number_format` MCP tool (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:397`) and `formatVnd`, which calls `formatNumber` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts:36`). The behaviour is not documented.

## Fix

Round the shortest round-trip decimal string of the number (`String(abs)`, e.g. `"2.675"`) half away from zero, using string or BigInt arithmetic on the digits, not floating-point maths. Keep these paths unchanged:

- `abs >= 1e21`: keep the existing BigInt path
- `String(abs)` in exponent notation (very small numbers such as `1e-7`): fall back to the current `toFixed` behaviour

Only change the rounding step. Grouping, the comma decimal mark, trailing-zero trimming and the negative-zero handling must not change.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `formatNumber(2.675, { maxFractionDigits: 2 })` → `2,68`
- [ ] `formatNumber(1.005, { maxFractionDigits: 2 })` → `1,01`
- [ ] `formatNumber(-2.675, { maxFractionDigits: 2 })` → `-2,68`
- [ ] `formatNumber(0.5, { maxFractionDigits: 0 })` → `1` and `formatNumber(-0.004, { maxFractionDigits: 2 })` → `0` (no `-0`)
- [ ] `formatNumber(1e25)` still gives `10.000.000.000.000.000.905.969.664`
- [ ] These cases are added to `tests/golden/vn-number-format.json`; all existing golden and unit cases still pass, or any changed expectation is explained in the PR
- [ ] The JSDoc on `formatNumber` states the rounding rule (half away from zero on the shortest decimal representation)
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: Amounts on invoices and quotes that look wrong by one unit in the last place erode trust in a formatting library. It is a small, contained change with clear golden cases.

proposals.title: repo: add an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifest (root plugin.json + mcp.json) so Cursor and Codex load vn-skills as a plugin
proposals.body:
## Problem

Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (https://agent-plugins.org) is a vendor-neutral plugin format. Its steering committee includes Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI and Vercel. Cursor's docs say plugins that follow the spec load in Cursor (https://cursor.com/docs/plugins). OpenAI's docs say a root `plugin.json` is now the preferred manifest for ChatGPT/Codex plugins, with `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` kept as a fallback (https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins).

vn-skills ships only the Claude Code plugin files: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and an unversioned `.mcp.json`. There is no root `plugin.json` and no root `mcp.json`. The skills are already where the spec expects them (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), so only the two manifests are missing.

What the spec requires (from https://agent-plugins.org/plugin-authors/build-an-agent-plugin and https://agent-plugins.org/plugin-authors/mcp-servers):

- `plugin.json` at the repo root with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`, a kebab-case `name`, `version` and `description`. Skills under `skills/` need no manifest field.
- `mcp.json` at the repo root with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json"` and only an `mcpServers` object. Each server needs `"type": "stdio"` and `command` as a single executable token.

## What to add

`plugin.json`:
- `name`: `vn-skills`
- `version`: the current root `package.json` version
- `description`: reuse the text from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- `license`, `homepage` and `repository`: same values as `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, only where the schema allows these fields

`mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "vn-skills": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp@<exact version>"] }
  }
}
```

## Version sync

Both version fields must move with each release. Add `plugin.json` `$.version` to `extra-files` in `release-please-config.json`; the existing `json` updater handles that. The pinned `@vn-skills/mcp@<version>` string in `mcp.json` has the same sync problem as `.mcp.json` in #154. Use whatever mechanism #154 adopts, so both files are updated the same way. Do this after #154 is merged, or in the same PR if the maintainer agrees.

This issue explicitly allows the `release-please-config.json` change.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` exist with the fields above and end with a newline
- [ ] `tests/plugin.test.ts` gains tests checking:
  - [ ] `plugin.json` has the 1.0.0 schema URL, `name === 'vn-skills'`, and `version` equal to root `package.json` `version`
  - [ ] `mcp.json` has only `$schema` and `mcpServers`, the server has `type: 'stdio'` and `command: 'npx'`, and its args pin `@vn-skills/mcp@` to the version in `packages/mcp/package.json`
- [ ] `release-please-config.json` updates `plugin.json` `$.version`, and `mcp.json`'s pin uses the same mechanism as #154
- [ ] `.claude-plugin/*` and `.mcp.json` are unchanged by this PR, apart from any change #154 makes to them
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: one short line under "Install the skills" saying the repo is also an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plugin (Cursor/Codex), with a link to agent-plugins.org
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The project has 0 stars but about 2k monthly npm downloads, so the reach comes from install channels, not GitHub discovery. One standard manifest makes the existing skills + MCP server installable as a plugin in Cursor and Codex, and is a prerequisite for their plugin directories.

proposals.title: docs: add a Codex repo marketplace entry and get vn-skills listed in the Codex/ChatGPT and Cursor plugin directories
proposals.body:
## Problem

Once the repo ships an Agent Plugins manifest (see the issue "repo: add an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifest (root plugin.json + mcp.json)…"), three distribution steps remain. Each needs a real client, an account or a value the repo doesn't contain:

1. **Codex repo marketplace.** Codex users can run `codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo`, which reads `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` (https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins). Each entry needs `source`, `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication` and `category`. A plugin at the repo root uses `"source": "url"`. The allowed values for `policy.*` and `category` are not recorded in this repo, and the file has to be tested with a current Codex CLI.
2. **OpenAI's public plugin directory**, shared by ChatGPT and Codex. How to submit is not confirmed: https://developers.openai.com/plugins/publish returned 404, and the docs only describe workspace publishing and repo marketplaces.
3. **Cursor.** The official Cursor Marketplace is manually reviewed and submitted through the Cursor team (https://cursor.com/docs/plugins). Community plugins and MCP servers are listed on cursor.directory, which returned 429 when checked, so it is unknown whether vn-skills is already listed.

This is related to #164 (which folder Codex reads skills from): a plugin install would make that question moot for plugin users.

## Checklist

- [ ] Read https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins and https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins.md and note the allowed values for `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication` and `category`
- [ ] Add `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` with one `vn-skills` entry (`"source": "url"` pointing at https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills), ending with a newline. Add a test in `tests/plugin.test.ts` that checks the entry's required keys exist
- [ ] Run `codex plugin marketplace add beiryu/vn-skills` with a current Codex CLI, install the plugin, ask "tạo QR chuyển 500k vào VCB số tài khoản 0011001234567", and confirm the `vietqr` skill and the MCP tools load
- [ ] Find the current submission route for OpenAI's public plugin directory and submit, or note here that none exists yet
- [ ] Check cursor.directory for vn-skills and submit the plugin / MCP server if it is not listed
- [ ] Decide whether to apply to the official Cursor Marketplace and record the outcome here
- [ ] When listed, add the Codex marketplace command to README.md and README.vi.md under "Install the skills"
proposals.rationale: [needs you] Directory listings are where the current npm-only traction can turn into discoverable installs, and the Codex and Cursor directories have no Vietnam toolkit. The marketplace values and submissions need a real Codex install and accounts, so a person has to do this.

proposals.title: docs: say that GitHub Copilot loads skills from .agents/skills and .claude/skills
proposals.body:
## Problem
GitHub's and VS Code's docs (read 2026-10-24) say Agent Skills work in Copilot: VS Code agent mode, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review.

- Copilot loads project skills from `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills`.
- It loads personal skills from `~/.copilot/skills` or `~/.agents/skills`.
- Personal skills are not available to the cloud agent.

Sources:
- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/customizations/agent-skills
- https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills
- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/customize-cloud-agent/add-skills

So `vn-skills install all --agent agents` and `--agent claude` already work for Copilot users. Our docs never say so. These four places list Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI as readers of `.agents/skills/`, and Copilot is not mentioned anywhere in the repo:

- `README.md:75`
- `README.vi.md:73`
- `docs/quickstart.md:121`
- `docs/quickstart.vi.md:121`

## Acceptance
- [ ] `README.md` and `docs/quickstart.md`: add GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI, cloud agent) to the list of agents that read `.agents/skills/`. Link https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/customizations/agent-skills.
- [ ] Same change in Vietnamese in `README.vi.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md`.
- [ ] Add one sentence to all four files: for the Copilot cloud agent, install in project scope (`--agent agents` without `--global`), because the cloud agent does not load personal skills.
- [ ] No code changes. `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes, and `pnpm format:check` passes.
proposals.rationale: Copilot is probably the agent with the most users, and our install paths already work for it. Saying so in the README costs one line, and with 0 stars and about 700 npm downloads a month, reach is what moves adoption now.

proposals.title: cli: add `install --agent copilot` (.github/skills, or ~/.copilot/skills with --global)
proposals.body:
## Problem
`packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts` maps only `claude`, `cursor`, `codex` and `agents` (lines 8-11 and the `--agent` help at line 27). According to GitHub's docs, Copilot's own skill locations are:

- project: `.github/skills`
- personal: `~/.copilot/skills`

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/customizations/agent-skills, read 2026-10-24.

Copilot users who look for their agent's name in `--agent` find nothing. `--agent agents` works for them, but they have to know that.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `--agent copilot` installs to `<cwd>/.github/skills/<name>` in project scope and to `~/.copilot/skills/<name>` with `--global`. Note that the project folder is `.github`, not `.copilot`, so the current `<base>/skills` mapping needs a per-scope special case.
- [ ] The `--agent` help text lists `copilot`.
- [ ] `--force` and `--dry-run` behave the same as for the other agents.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` use a temp dir and cover the project path, the `--global` path (with HOME redirected the same way the existing install tests do it) and `--dry-run`.
- [ ] Add `copilot` to the `--agent` list in `README.md`, `README.vi.md`, `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` passes.
proposals.rationale: Users look for their own agent's name in `--agent`. A first-class Copilot target makes the install command match what they expect.

proposals.title: docs: check `gh skill publish --dry-run` and document `gh skill install beiryu/vn-skills`
proposals.body:
## Problem
GitHub CLI has these skill commands:

- `gh skill search`
- `gh skill preview OWNER/REPO SKILL`
- `gh skill install OWNER/REPO [SKILL][@TAG|@SHA]`, with `--agent` and `--scope user`

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/customize-cloud-agent/add-skills.

Our skills already live in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and releases are tagged. So `gh skill install beiryu/vn-skills vietqr@v<version>` should work, and it would be an install path that needs only `gh`, not Node.

None of this is confirmed yet:
- whether the repo passes `gh skill publish --dry-run`
- what `publish` adds beyond validation
- how `gh skill search` finds repos

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] With a current `gh`, run `gh skill publish --dry-run` in the repo root and record the output in this issue.
- [ ] Fix any repository settings it flags (tag protection, secret scanning, code scanning), or record why not.
- [ ] Run `gh skill install beiryu/vn-skills vietqr@<latest tag> --agent claude-code` and confirm the skill loads.
- [ ] Decide whether to run `gh skill publish`, and record what it does.

proposals.title: docs: submit vn-skills to github/awesome-copilot as an external plugin
proposals.body:
## Problem
GitHub's docs point to `github/awesome-copilot` as the community collection of skills. Its CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-24) says plugins hosted elsewhere are submitted through an "external plugin" issue form, not a PR. The form asks for:

- plugin name
- short description
- `owner/repo`
- path (`/` for the repo root)
- release tag and the full 40-character commit SHA
- semver version
- SPDX license
- author
- lowercase hyphenated keywords

Automated validation runs first, then a maintainer reviews. The plugin manifest must be the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 root `plugin.json`, so this depends on #171. Copilot CLI installs plugins from that list.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/awesome-copilot/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

This is separate from #172, which covers the Codex/ChatGPT and Cursor directories.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Wait until #171 is merged and released, so a tagged release contains a valid root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json`.
- [ ] Check that awesome-copilot has no Vietnam entry already.
- [ ] Open the "external plugin" issue form in github/awesome-copilot with:
  - name `vn-skills`
  - repo `beiryu/vn-skills`, path `/`
  - the release tag and its full commit SHA
  - the released version
  - license `MIT`
  - author
  - keywords such as `vietnam`, `vietqr`, `vietnamese-address`, `tax-id`, `lunar-calendar`, `e-invoice`
- [ ] Link the submission here and fix any problems the automated validation reports.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] awesome-copilot is the collection GitHub's own docs point to. A listing puts vn-skills in front of Copilot CLI users, and offline Vietnam-specific validation is the kind of domain gap the list says it accepts.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: return INVALID_TIMEZONE instead of ok:true with day:null for a non-numeric timeZone
proposals.body:
## Problem
These exported functions take a public `timeZone` parameter (default `VN_TIMEZONE`) and never validate it:

- `lunarInfo` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:54-59`)
- `solarToLunar` (`packages/core/src/lunar/convert.ts:122-126`)
- `lunarToSolar` (`convert.ts:181-186`)

A string such as `'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'`, `NaN` or `Infinity` turns the new-moon arithmetic into NaN, but the result still says success:

```
lunarInfo(10, 2, 2024, 'x' as any)
→ {"ok":true,"day":null,"month":1,"year":2024,...,"yearCanChi":"Giáp Thìn",...}
```

Every other core module returns `{ ok: false, error }` for bad input. Only library callers are affected: the CLI and MCP tools do not expose a timezone option.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `solarToLunar`, `lunarToSolar` and `lunarInfo` return `fail('INVALID_TIMEZONE', …)` with a `hint` when `timeZone` is not a finite number in the UTC offset range -12 to +14 (hours). The hint should say the value is a UTC offset in hours, e.g. `7` for Vietnam.
- [ ] `leapMonthOf` and `lunarMonthLength`, which return `number | null`, return `null` for an invalid `timeZone` instead of computing with NaN.
- [ ] Omitting `timeZone`, or passing `VN_TIMEZONE` or `7`, gives exactly the same results as today. All existing tests and `tests/golden/vn-lunar.json` still pass.
- [ ] New tests in `tests/lunar.test.ts` cover a string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-13`, `15`, a valid non-VN offset (`8`), and `lunarToSolar` with a bad timeZone.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` passes.
proposals.rationale: A library call that silently returns `ok:true` with `day:null` breaks the documented contract that bad input gets an `ok:false` result, and callers that trust `ok` will use a wrong date. The fix is small and local.

proposals.title: vietqr: find the CRC tag by position so a payload whose CRC is 6304 parses as valid
proposals.body:
## Problem
`parseVietQR` locates the CRC field with `payload.lastIndexOf('6304')` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/parse.ts:46`). When the 4-hex-digit CRC value is itself `6304`, the last match is the CRC value, not the tag header. The CRC is then computed over the wrong prefix, so `crcValid` is `false` and a bogus warning is added. This affects about 1 in 65,536 payloads, including ones `buildVietQR` produced itself, so build → parse does not round-trip. Callers that gate on `crcValid` reject a correct code.

Reproduction (amount found by looping `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',amount:i})` until `crc === '6304'`):

```
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: 148444 }).payload
// 00020101021238470010A0000007270117000697043601031230208QRIBFTTA530370454061484445802VN63046304
parseVietQR(payload)
// crcValid: false, warnings: ['CRC mismatch: payload has 6304, expected FA09.']
```

The lower-case detection branch just below (lines 50-58) uses the same `crcIndex` and has the same flaw.

## Fix
Take the CRC position from the structure, not a substring search. For example, when the last top-level TLV node is tag `63` with length `04`, the tag header starts at `payload.length - 8`. Check `payload.slice(-8, -4).toUpperCase() === '6304'` and hash `payload.slice(0, payload.length - 4)`. Keep the existing behaviour for payloads where tag 63 is missing or not last (the `CRC tag 63 is not the last field.` warning).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseVietQR` of the amount-148444 payload above returns `ok: true`, `crcValid: true` and no CRC warning
- [ ] Golden case added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` for that payload (pure input → output)
- [ ] A test that builds the amount-148444 payload with `buildVietQR` and checks the parse round-trips
- [ ] The lower-cased-payload warning (#131 behaviour) still works, including for a lower-cased payload whose CRC is `6304`
- [ ] Existing vietqr tests pass; `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint` clean
proposals.rationale: This is a correctness bug in the flagship skill: the toolkit rejects its own valid output, which undermines its main promise of validating payloads. The fix is small and the test case is already known.

proposals.title: cli: make `address convert-file` errors honour --json with READ_ERROR / COLUMN_NOT_FOUND codes
proposals.body:
## Problem
`vn-skills address convert-file` uses a local `fail()` helper (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts:156-159`) that always writes `Error: ...` to stderr as plain text, even with `--json`. Every other command returns `{ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}}` through `failExit` (`packages/cli/src/output.ts:23`). Examples are `vietqr decode` (`READ_ERROR` in `packages/cli/src/decode.ts`) and `einvoice validate` (`READ_ERROR` in `packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts`). Agents that parse stdout get nothing.

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file nofile
Error: cannot read nofile: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'nofile'   (exit 1)
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file tmp.csv --csv --column nope
Error: column "nope" not found in CSV header (name, address)   (exit 1)
```

Three paths are affected: `--csv` without `--column` (line 160), an unreadable file (line 168) and an unknown column (line 176).

## Fix
Replace the local `fail` with `failExit(c, {code, message, hint})`. Add the `Command` argument to the `.action` callback, as the other subcommands do. Suggested codes: `MISSING_COLUMN` (`--csv` without `--column`), `READ_ERROR` (file cannot be read), `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` (header lacks the column; the hint lists the available columns). Keep exit code 1 for these, and exit code 2 for "some rows failed".

## Acceptance
- [ ] With `--json`, all three cases print the `{ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}}` JSON on stdout and exit 1
- [ ] Without `--json` on a TTY, they print `Error [CODE]: ...` and `Hint: ...` like other commands
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` for each of the three cases (use a temp dir for the CSV)
- [ ] Exit code 2 for partial row failures is unchanged
- [ ] `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint` clean
proposals.rationale: `convert-file` is the newest command and covers the main address job: bulk-migrating old addresses. Agents depend on the JSON error shape, and this command is the only one that breaks it.

proposals.title: mcp: add a Dockerfile that runs the stdio MCP server, as needed for the Docker MCP Catalog
proposals.body:
## Problem
Docker's MCP registry (`docker/mcp-registry`) feeds hub.docker.com/mcp and Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit. Its CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-24) says local (stdio) servers need a Dockerfile in the source repo. The submission tooling builds that image, runs it and checks that it lists tools. vn-skills has no `Dockerfile` or `.dockerignore`, so it cannot be submitted. The server is offline and needs no secrets or env config, which keeps the image simple.

## What to build
- A root `Dockerfile` that builds `@vn-skills/mcp` from this workspace, so the version always matches the commit Docker pins and no release-sync step is needed:
  - Node 22 base image (an `-alpine` or `-slim` variant is fine)
  - `corepack enable`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, then a slim runtime stage with only what `packages/mcp/dist/index.js` needs at runtime (core `dist` + `data`, prod deps)
  - Run as a non-root user
  - `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "packages/mcp/dist/index.js"]` (or the equivalent path in the runtime stage), stdio transport, no exposed ports
- A root `.dockerignore` that excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist` build outputs, tests and docs not needed for the build
- A short "Docker" subsection under "MCP client setup" in `README.md` and `README.vi.md`: `docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` plus a client config using `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp`

Do not change `.github/workflows/` or release config in this issue.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` succeeds from a clean checkout
- [ ] Sending `initialize` then `tools/list` JSON-RPC lines to `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp` returns the 28 tools (state in the PR if Docker was not available to run this)
- [ ] The container makes no network calls at runtime and needs no env vars
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md updated in both languages; files end with a newline
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm lint` clean
proposals.rationale: npm downloads (858/month for the MCP server) are the only traction signal, and they come from MCP users. Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit is a large MCP channel where vn-skills is absent, and a Dockerfile is the only missing prerequisite.

proposals.title: docs: submit vn-skills to the Docker MCP Catalog (docker/mcp-registry)
proposals.body:

proposals.title: cli: reject install --agent values that are Object.prototype keys with the Unknown agent error
proposals.body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts` stores the agent folders in an ordinary object literal (`const AGENT_DIRS: Record<string, string> = { claude: '.claude', ... }`, lines 7-13). The `install` action looks up `AGENT_DIRS[o.agent]` and only checks that the result is truthy (`if (!agentDir) throw new Error('Unknown agent ...')`).

For agent names that are inherited `Object.prototype` keys (`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__`, ...), the lookup returns a function or `Object.prototype`, which is truthy. The check is skipped, and the command then fails inside `path.join` with an error that never mentions the agent:

```text
$ cd /tmp && node <repo>/packages/cli/dist/index.js install all --agent constructor --dry-run
The "path" argument must be of type string. Received function Object
```

The intended message, `Unknown agent "constructor". Use one of: claude, cursor, codex, agents, copilot`, is never shown. `tests/cli.test.ts` only covers an invalid agent named `nope` (around line 538).

## Fix

Look the agent up only among its own keys, for example `Object.hasOwn(AGENT_DIRS, o.agent) ? AGENT_DIRS[o.agent] : undefined`, or turn `AGENT_DIRS` into a `Map`. Do the same for any other lookup in this file that indexes `AGENT_DIRS` with user input, including the special case that maps `copilot` to `.github` in project scope. The list of valid agents and their target folders stays the same.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `install vietqr --agent constructor`, `--agent toString`, `--agent hasOwnProperty` and `--agent __proto__` exit non-zero and print `Unknown agent "<name>". Use one of: claude, cursor, codex, agents, copilot` on stderr. With `--dry-run` they also write nothing.
- [ ] New cases in `tests/cli.test.ts` next to the existing unknown-agent test cover these names. They fail on the current code.
- [ ] The existing install tests for claude, cursor, codex, agents and copilot still pass.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: `install` is the main way people adopt the skills. A crash that doesn't name the bad agent is a confusing first experience, and the fix is a single line.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts:7-13","packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts:37-41","tests/cli.test.ts:536-542","$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js install all --agent constructor --dry-run -> The \"path\" argument must be of type string. Received function Object"]

proposals.title: docs: update the Glama listing summary to all 11 skills and get the MIT licence graded

proposals.title: docs: add llms-install.md so Cline can set up the MCP server from the repo alone
proposals.body:
## Problem

Cline's MCP Marketplace (https://github.com/cline/mcp-marketplace) asks submitters to confirm that Cline can install the server by itself, using `README.md` or an optional `llms-install.md` at the repo root. The repo has no `llms-install.md`. The MCP setup in `README.md` is mixed in with skills, the CLI and other clients, so it is harder for an agent to follow than one short, MCP-only guide.

The server needs no API keys or env vars and runs over stdio with `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp` (Node.js 22+). The repo already documents all of this in README.md under "MCP server" and "MCP client setup".

## What to add

A root `llms-install.md`, in English, written for an AI agent that is installing the MCP server. Copy the facts from `README.md`; do not add new ones.

- Requirements: Node.js 22+, no accounts, API keys or env vars; the server is offline.
- The `mcpServers` config block exactly as in README.md: `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`. If #154 has landed and the repo pins the version elsewhere, use that same pin and the same release-sync mechanism here; otherwise keep it unpinned like README.md.
- How to check it worked: the server prints `vn-skills MCP server running on stdio` to stderr, and lists 28 tools. Take the tool count from README.md, and say tools are grouped by skill (vietqr, vn-address, …).
- One example prompt that calls a tool, taken from the README examples (e.g. build a VietQR for VCB, or convert `P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM`).
- The Docker alternative from README.md (`docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` then `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp`).
- A one-line note that it is an offline toolkit, not a payment gateway (same wording as the README).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `llms-install.md` exists at the repo root and ends with a newline
- [ ] Its JSON config block parses and has the same `command`/`args` as the README `mcpServers` block
- [ ] A test in `tests/readme.test.ts` (or a new small test file) checks the two points above and that the tool count it states matches the number of `registerTool(` calls in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md link to it from the MCP client setup section (one line each)
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The Cline MCP Marketplace is a channel where vn-skills isn't listed yet. Its submission asks submitters to confirm that Cline can install the server on its own, and a short guide makes that more reliable. With 0 stars, getting listed in another directory is one of the few things that can bring in users.

proposals.title: docs: make a 400×400 PNG logo and submit vn-skills to the Cline MCP Marketplace
proposals.body:
## Problem

vn-skills is not in Cline's MCP Marketplace (https://github.com/cline/mcp-marketplace), which lists servers for one-click install in Cline. The submission is an issue form (`mcp-server-submission.yml`). It needs a GitHub repo URL, a **400×400 PNG logo**, a reason for adding the server, and confirmation that Cline installed the server by itself from `README.md` or `llms-install.md`. The repo has no logo or icon PNG anywhere.

Reviewers look at adoption, maintainer credibility, maturity and security, and they look harder at financial projects. VietQR falls under that, so the reason for adding the server should point to the README's "offline toolkit, not a payment gateway" statement. Their FAQ says servers with few stars can still be accepted.

The same logo can also be used for the Glama (#188), Anthropic plugin directory (#155) and Docker catalog (#186) listings.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Make a 400×400 PNG logo and commit it (e.g. `assets/logo.png`; the trademark rules in TRADEMARK.md apply, so no NAPAS/VietQR or bank marks)
- [ ] Wait for the `llms-install.md` issue to land
- [ ] In Cline, ask it to install the MCP server from https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills and confirm it works (for example a `vietqr_build` call and a `vn_address_convert` call)
- [ ] Open the submission issue on cline/mcp-marketplace with the repo URL, the logo, and a reason that mentions: offline, no API keys, 11 Vietnam-specific skills / 28 tools, and that it is not a payment gateway
- [ ] Link the submission issue here and close this once it is listed
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This is a new directory listing for Cline users and needs no code, only a logo and a submission. Making the logo also helps the other directory listings that are still in progress.

proposals.title: docs: submit vn-skills to mcp.so and position it as the offline, no-credentials option
proposals.body:
## Problem

mcp.so is a large MCP directory. Its own submit page claims 2.2M unique visitors over 12 months and 266K monthly active users. On 2026-10-25, searching it for `vn-skills` returned nothing, and none of its 7 `vietnam` results is vn-skills. Nothing in the repo mentions mcp.so.

Two of the Vietnam listings there overlap with what vn-skills does:

- **monapay-mcp** (themonagroup) creates VietQR codes as part of MONA Pay: it checks incoming bank transfers, runs webhooks and sends Zalo notifications.
- **Vietnam Invoice** (junter1989k-ai) issues e-invoices through MISA meInvoice. It is a hosted HTTP endpoint that needs the user's MISA token and tax code in request headers.

Both are online services that need an account. vn-skills is offline and needs no credentials. It builds and validates VietQR payloads and checks e-invoices against the schema, but it does not collect payments or issue invoices. Without a listing, people searching mcp.so for Vietnam tools only find the account-based options.

The submit form at https://mcp.so/submit?type=server asks for a repository URL and an optional name. A $39 one-time fee is optional; it buys immediate publishing without review, a verified badge and a dofollow link. The free path appears to go through review, and how long that takes is unknown.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Decide between the free reviewed submission and the paid $39 option.
- [ ] Submit https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills at https://mcp.so/submit?type=server with the name `vn-skills`.
- [ ] If the form or the claimed listing lets you edit the description, state plainly: offline, no API keys or accounts, 11 skills (VietQR, 34-province addresses, tax ID, CCCD, phone, holidays, money in words, lunar calendar, e-invoice schema, names, number formatting), not a payment gateway and does not issue invoices. Reuse the wording from the README section added in #118.
- [ ] Once it is live, check that the listing page shows the `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp` config block from the README. mcp.so parses that block from the README.
- [ ] Search https://mcp.so/search?q=vietnam and confirm vn-skills appears.

## Notes

This is the same kind of step as #186 (Docker MCP Catalog) and #194 (Cline Marketplace). It needs an account and possibly money, so a person has to do it.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] The repo has 0 stars, and the MCP package has the most npm downloads (858 a month), so directory listings are the cheapest discovery channel. On mcp.so, the Vietnam niche is currently shown only through account-based competitors.

proposals.title: vn-address: convert many addresses in one call (core function + vn_address_convert_batch MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem

Bulk conversion of old 63-province addresses is the main job for the address skill, and competing npm packages advertise CSV migration (see #156). vn-skills now has `vn-skills address convert-file` (#161), but that logic lives only in the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts`, the `convert-file <file>` command). Nothing is exported from `@vn-skills/core`, and there is no MCP tool for it.

The MCP tool `vn_address_convert` (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`, around line 200) takes one address per call. An agent working through MCP on a customer list therefore has to make one tool call per row. That is slow, uses a lot of context, and the agent has no summary of which rows failed. `@vn-skills/mcp` is the most-downloaded package (858 a month), so this gap affects the main way people use vn-skills.

This needs no new data or Vietnamese facts. It reuses `convertAddress` and the existing mapping.

## Proposal

1. **Core.** Add `convertAddresses(inputs)` in `packages/core/src/address/` and export it from `packages/core/src/index.ts`.
   - `inputs` is an array of free-text address strings.
   - It returns `{ ok: true, results, summary: { total, converted, failed } }`.
   - `results[i]` holds `index`, `input` and either the same fields `convert-file` emits per row or `{ ok: false, error }`.
   - It never throws for null, non-string or empty items; each such item becomes a per-row error.
   - A non-array argument returns a top-level `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_INPUT', ... } }`.
   - More than 1000 items returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'TOO_MANY', message, hint } }`. The hint points to `vn-skills address convert-file` for larger inputs.
2. **CLI.** Change `address convert-file` to call `convertAddresses` per chunk (or row), so the CLI and MCP share one code path. The NDJSON/CSV output and the exit code (2 when some rows fail) must stay exactly the same as today.
3. **MCP.** Add `vn_address_convert_batch` to `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` with input `{ addresses: string[] }` (zod array of strings, max 1000). It returns the core result as JSON. Describe it like `vn_address_convert` and name the 1000 limit.
4. **Docs.**
   - Add the tool to the `vn-address` row of the MCP tools table in `README.md` and `README.vi.md`, and change the tool count from 28 to 29.
   - Mention the batch tool in `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md`.
   - Update the MCP Registry description only if it lists tools (it should not need to change).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `convertAddresses` is exported from `@vn-skills/core`. Tests cover: a mixed batch with one row that converts and one unknown address, plus null, `''` and a number. Also an empty array (`total: 0`), 1001 items (`TOO_MANY`) and a non-array argument.
- [ ] For a sample batch, results match calling `convertAddress` on each item.
- [ ] Existing `address convert-file` tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` pass unchanged (same output and exit codes).
- [ ] `tests/mcp.test.ts` lists `vn_address_convert_batch` and calls it with 2 addresses, checking `summary.converted`/`summary.failed`.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md list the new tool and say 29 tools. `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: MCP is the most-downloaded package, and bulk 63→34 address migration is what address users come for. Right now an MCP agent must make one call per row. This reuses existing data and needs no new facts.

proposals.title: vietqr: check the 13-digit amount limit on the digit string, not on Number(amount)
proposals.body:
## Problem

`buildVietQR` converts the amount with `Number(raw)` and then checks `String(amount).length > 13` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:95-97`). For 21 or more digits, `String(Number)` switches to exponent notation, so the check sees a short string:

```
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: '9'.repeat(30) })
→ ok: true, payload ...54051e+305802VN6304 6F5A, amount 1e+30
```

Tag 54 is set to `1e+30`, which is not a valid EMVCo amount. `parseVietQR` on that payload also returns `ok: true` with a matching CRC, so a broken QR code gets through both steps. Amounts above 2^53 that are 14–20 digits long are already rejected by the length check, but the precision loss is a second reason to check before converting: `12345678901234567890` becomes `12345678901234567000`.

## Fix

Work on the digit string `raw` that `parseAmountString` returns:
- strip leading zeros
- reject an empty or all-zero result with the existing `Amount must be greater than 0` error
- reject more than 13 digits with the existing `INVALID_AMOUNT` / `Amount exceeds 13 digits allowed by EMVCo` error
- only then build the tag value. Use the stripped digit string so the payload never contains exponent notation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',amount:'9'.repeat(30)})` returns `ok:false` with code `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `amount: '12345678901234567890'` (20 digits) returns `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `amount: '9999999999999'` (13 digits) still builds, and tag 54 is exactly `9999999999999`
- [ ] `amount: '00500000'` builds with tag 54 = `500000`
- [ ] Golden cases for the 30-digit and 13-digit amounts are added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` (loaded by `tests/golden.ts`)
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The library reports a corrupt payment QR as valid at both build and parse time. That defeats the point of a validation toolkit, and the fix is a few lines.

proposals.title: mcp: return per-row errors for null or non-string entries in vn_address_convert_batch
proposals.body:
## Problem

`vn_address_convert_batch` declares `addresses: z.array(z.string()).max(1000)` (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:207`). A single `null` entry, for example an empty CSV cell sent as JSON, fails input validation for the whole call:

```
tools/call vn_address_convert_batch {"addresses":["Hà Nội",null,""]}
→ MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... expected string, received null at addresses[1]
```

The caller gets no row results at all. The tool description and `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` promise results for each row plus a summary `{ total, converted, failed }`. The core function `convertAddresses(inputs: unknown)` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:262`) already handles any array and returns a per-row result for each entry, so only the MCP schema gets in the way.

## Fix

Let each array entry be any value (e.g. `z.array(z.unknown()).max(1000)` or `z.array(z.string().nullable())`, whichever fits the SDK's JSON-schema output). Keep the 1000 limit. Pass the array straight to `convertAddresses` so bad entries come back as `ok:false` rows and are counted in `summary.failed`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` calls the tool with `["Hà Nội", null, ""]` and gets `ok:true`, three rows, row 1 `ok:false` with an error code, and a summary with `failed >= 1`
- [ ] More than 1000 entries is still rejected
- [ ] The tool description and `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` say that null or empty entries come back as failed rows
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The batch tool was just added (#198), and its main use, converting customer databases, regularly has missing cells. One null value should not discard the whole batch.

proposals.title: cli: exit quietly when stdout is closed early in `address convert-file` (EPIPE)
proposals.body:
## Problem

Piping `address convert-file` into a reader that stops early prints a Node stack trace and exits with status 1:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file big.txt | head -c 10
node:events:497
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
Error: write EPIPE
  code: 'EPIPE', syscall: 'write'
```

The line-by-line loop (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts:219-236`) calls `process.stdout.write` for every row, and nothing handles a stdout `error` event. Previewing a large file with `| head` is a normal thing to do.

## Fix

When stdout is closed by the reader (`EPIPE`), stop writing and exit quietly with status 0, the way other Unix-style tools do. Handle this once for the CLI, e.g. a `process.stdout.on('error', …)` handler in `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, so every command is covered. Other stdout errors should still be reported on stderr with exit code 1.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A test in `tests/cli.test.ts` runs `address convert-file` on a file with several hundred lines, with stdout piped into a reader that closes after the first bytes. It asserts that stderr has no `EPIPE` stack trace and the CLI exits with 0
- [ ] Normal `convert-file` output and its exit code 2 for failed rows are unchanged
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: Bulk conversion is the newest headline CLI feature. A stack trace on `| head` is the first thing a user previewing a file sees.

proposals.title: data: choose an official source for renamed banks (Vikki, Vietcombank Neo) and wallet BINs (ZaloPay, ViettelMoney, …)
proposals.body:
## Problem

`packages/core/data/banks.json` comes from `xuannghia/vietnam-qr-pay` (pinned `17a05d3`). Its only newer commit, `a7e5b89`, adds a MoMo icon, so refreshing from upstream fixes nothing below.

VietQR.io's public bank list (https://api.vietqr.io/v2/banks, fetched 2026-10-26) differs from `banks.json`:

1. **Renamed banks.**
   - BIN 970406: VietQR.io says `Vikki` (Ngân hàng TNHH Một thành viên số Vikki); `banks.json:113-116` says `DONGABANK` / DongA Bank.
   - BIN 970444: VietQR.io says Vietcombank Neo; `banks.json:445-448` says `VNCB` / CB Bank.
   - Neither new name is an alias, so `buildVietQR({bank:'Vikki'})` finds no bank, and decoding a QR code with these BINs shows the old name.
2. **Missing wallet and digital-bank BINs.** VietQR.io lists these, and `banks.json` has none of them:
   - ZaloPay 971101
   - MVAS/MobiFone 971032
   - PVcomBank Pay 971133
   - ViettelMoney 971005
   - VNPTMoney 971011

   VietQR codes that pay into ZaloPay are common and decode with an unknown bank today. This may also cover part of #119.

VietQR.io is a third-party service (Casso), not NAPAS or the State Bank of Vietnam. Under the project rules, these names and BINs cannot go into the data until a maintainer confirms them from a citable source.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Confirm the 970406 and 970444 renames from an official source (e.g. State Bank of Vietnam decisions on the transfer of DongA Bank and CBBank) and record the URLs
- [ ] Confirm the wallet/digital-bank BINs from a NAPAS or SBV source, or decide that VietQR.io is acceptable as a cited secondary source
- [ ] Choose a route:
  - (a) open a PR upstream at xuannghia/vietnam-qr-pay and bump the pin, or
  - (b) add a second pinned/dated source to `scripts/build-data.ts` that adds aliases/new names and new BINs on top of upstream
- [ ] Once the source is decided, open a follow-up implementation issue that names the source. The data changes must go through `pnpm build-data` and `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md` and keep old names as aliases. They also need golden cases in `tests/golden/vietqr.json` for `bank: 'Vikki'` and BIN 971101.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] Users asking for a QR to Vikki, Vietcombank Neo or ZaloPay get no match today. The fix needs a sourcing decision, which only the maintainer can make.

proposals.title: docs: find out how github.com/mcp picks servers and get vn-skills listed
proposals.body:
## Problem

On 2026-10-26, GitHub's MCP registry API returned `count 0` for `vn-skills` (https://api.mcp.github.com/v0.1/servers?search=vn-skills). A search for `playwright` returns `microsoft/playwright-mcp`, so the endpoint works. GitHub's entries add their own metadata (displayName, nameWithOwner, license, preferredImage), so it is a curated list and not a copy of registry.modelcontextprotocol.io. vn-skills has been in the official registry since 0.6.0 (`io.github.beiryu/vn-skills`, now 0.7.0), and it still isn't listed. This list feeds the MCP server browser at github.com/mcp that Copilot and VS Code users see. We already target Copilot users with `install --agent copilot`.

I could not find how entries are chosen or whether there is a submission path: the docs page tried returned 404, and github.com/mcp renders in the browser, so its contents could not be fetched.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Find GitHub's documentation for the MCP registry at github.com/mcp (selection criteria, submission form or partner process)
- [ ] If there is a submission path, submit `beiryu/vn-skills` with the `@vn-skills/mcp` npm package and the existing `packages/mcp/server.json` metadata. Describe it as offline, needing no credentials, and covering 11 skills
- [ ] If entries are invite-only, record that on this issue and close it
- [ ] Re-run `https://api.mcp.github.com/v0.1/servers?search=vn-skills` and paste the result
proposals.rationale: [needs you] Stars are 0 and almost all npm traffic comes from listings. GitHub's MCP browser reaches Copilot users directly, and it is the only big directory where nobody has yet checked how to get listed.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: pick a cited reference for giờ hoàng đạo, trực and nạp âm before implementing them
proposals.body:
## Problem

People in Vietnam ask agents questions like "giờ hoàng đạo hôm nay" and "ngày này tốt không" (lucky hours today; is this a good day). `vn-lunar` already does solar ↔ lunar conversion, can chi and solar terms (`packages/core/src/lunar`, `solarTerm`/`SOLAR_TERMS`). A grep of `packages/core/src/lunar` and `skills/vn-lunar` finds no giờ hoàng đạo, trực or nạp âm.

The most-found Vietnamese lunar package on npm, `react-native-lich-am` (MIT, 1.0.2), lists all three plus ngày tốt xấu (searches for 'am lich vietnam' and 'lich am can chi', 2026-10-26). Users comparing the two will notice the gap.

Each feature rests on traditional lookup tables (for example, which hours are hoàng đạo for each day's chi, the 12 trực, and the 60 nạp âm). The repo contains none of them. Under the project rules they must not be copied from a competitor's code or written from memory.

## Checklist (maintainer)

- [ ] Pick a citable reference for each table: giờ hoàng đạo by day chi, 12 trực, 60-entry nạp âm. Record the title, edition or URL, and the licence
- [ ] Decide scope: giờ hoàng đạo / trực / nạp âm only, or also a "ngày tốt xấu" verdict (which is more interpretive)
- [ ] Open an implementation issue that quotes the tables' source and specifies:
  - a core function (e.g. `luckyHours(date)`, `dayOfficer(date)`, `napAm(canChi)`)
  - CLI `vn-skills lunar …` subcommands
  - an MCP tool
  - `skills/vn-lunar/SKILL.md` updates with the Vietnamese trigger words
  - ≥ 20 tests
  - golden cases in `tests/golden/`
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This is a common everyday question that agents get wrong, and the nearest competitor already answers it. It is blocked only on a sourcing decision.

proposals.title: repo: add npm keywords for lunar features vn-skills already has (can-chi, tiet-khi, lich-am, lich-viet)
proposals.body:
## Problem

People searching npm for a Vietnamese lunar calendar use terms like `am-lich`, `can-chi`, `tiet-khi` and `lich-viet`. The top result for 'am lich vietnam' (`react-native-lich-am`) uses these keywords. `@vn-skills/core` and `@vn-skills/mcp` currently have only `am-lich` and `lunar` for this area. vn-lunar already does can chi and solar terms (tiết khí), so the packages miss searches for features they already have.

## Fix

Add the keywords `can-chi`, `tiet-khi`, `lich-am` and `lich-viet` to `packages/core/package.json`, `packages/mcp/package.json` and `packages/cli/package.json`, without duplicates. Do **not** add keywords for features that don't exist yet (e.g. `gio-hoang-dao`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] The three package.json files contain `am-lich`, `can-chi`, `tiet-khi`, `lich-am` and `lich-viet`
- [ ] `tests/package-metadata.test.ts` asserts that these keywords are present in all three packages
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: npm search is where most of the roughly 700–850 monthly downloads come from. Matching the search terms Vietnamese developers use costs nothing and only advertises features that already exist.

proposals.title: vn-number-format: add a hint to the INVALID_NUMBER error from formatNumber and formatCompactVnd
proposals.body:
## Problem
README.md says every error has the shape `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, hint } }`. The `numfmt format` path breaks this:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json numfmt format abc
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_NUMBER","message":"Value must be a finite number"}}
```

There is no `hint`. Other errors already have one, including `INVALID_OPTION` in the same function, `numfmt parse` and `money words`.

The cause is in `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`:
- line 28 (`formatNumber`): `if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return fail('INVALID_NUMBER', NOT_FINITE);`
- line 55 (`formatCompactVnd`): the same call

`formatVnd` calls `formatNumber`, so it returns the same error without a hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatNumber`, `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` return `INVALID_NUMBER` with a non-empty `hint` for `NaN`, `Infinity` and non-numeric input. The hint should say to pass a plain number such as `1234567.89`.
- [ ] Use one shared hint constant, as `NOT_FINITE` is for the message.
- [ ] `numfmt format abc` (CLI) and the `vn_number_format` MCP tool show the hint in their JSON output.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` check that `hint` is present for each of the three functions. If `tests/golden/vn-number-format.json` can express error cases, add a golden case for `format abc`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Agents rely on the documented {code,message,hint} error shape to recover. This is the one remaining numfmt path without a hint, and the fix is a few lines.

proposals.title: vietqr: warn when buildVietQR removes whitespace from the account number
proposals.body:
## Problem
`buildVietQR` removes all whitespace from the account without saying so (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:76`):

```ts
const account = String(opts.account ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, '');
```

A mistyped account is silently turned into a different one, and the result shows no sign of the change:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json vietqr build --bank VCB --account 'abc def'
{"ok":true,"payload":"...0106abcdef...","account":"abcdef",...,"warnings":[]}
```

Removing spaces is useful because people paste grouped numbers like `0011 0012 34567`. But a QR that pays a changed account should say so, the same way a sanitized note already adds `Note was sanitized ...`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] When the trimmed input differs from the account after spaces are removed, `buildVietQR` keeps building the QR and adds a warning to `warnings`. The warning names both values, e.g. `Spaces removed from account "abc def" -> "abcdef"; check the account number.`
- [ ] Leading and trailing whitespace alone (e.g. `' 0011001234567 '`) does not trigger the warning.
- [ ] Input without spaces keeps `warnings: []` (no regression for the existing golden cases).
- [ ] The warning shows in `vn-skills vietqr build` JSON output and in the `vietqr_build` MCP tool result.
- [ ] Add a golden case to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` for an account with inner spaces, plus a test in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` asserting the warning text.
- [ ] `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` "common mistakes" mentions that spaces are removed and a warning is returned.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: A payment QR that silently pays a changed account number undermines trust in vietqr, the flagship skill. A warning costs nothing and keeps the convenience.

proposals.title: mcp: decide whether to serve SKILL.md files over the MCP Skills extension (SEP-2640)
proposals.body:
## Problem
`@vn-skills/mcp` exposes tools only. A grep of `packages/mcp/src` finds no `registerResource`, `registerPrompt`, `SKILL.md` or extension use. MCP users therefore get none of the guidance in `skills/*/SKILL.md`: Vietnamese trigger words, common mistakes, "format validity ≠ identity exists" warnings.

The official SDK now ships as `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.4.0. It exports `./ext/skills`, which implements the MCP Skills extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`; `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read`). Limits are 512 files and 16 MiB per skill, and helpers such as `memorySkillFiles`, `skillEntry` and `SkillCatalog` build entries in memory. `packages/mcp/package.json` still depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.32.1.

Serving the skills over MCP would give every MCP install the skill guidance without copying any folders. Before any code is written, we need to know whether the extension is stable and which clients use it.

Sources:
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/server/latest
- https://unpkg.com/@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.4.0/dist/ext/skills/index.d.mts
- https://unpkg.com/@modelcontextprotocol/core@2.4.0/dist/ext/skills/index.mjs

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Find SEP-2640 in the MCP spec repo and record whether it is draft, accepted or final.
- [ ] Check whether Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code/Copilot and Cursor call `skills/list` today. Note each with a link.
- [ ] Estimate the work to move from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.x to the 2.x split packages: check that `tests/mcp.test.ts` and the Dockerfile still work.
- [ ] Decide one of: (a) migrate and serve skills via the extension; (b) stay on 1.x and wait; (c) another option. Record the decision here.
- [ ] If (a): open an implementation issue with concrete acceptance (which skills, how SKILL.md is bundled into the mcp package, tests).
proposals.rationale: [needs you] With 858 downloads/month, the MCP server is the most-installed package, and its users never see the SKILL.md guidance. Whether the extension is stable has to be confirmed before anyone starts a migration.

proposals.title: docs: check whether vn-skills is on the LobeHub MCP marketplace and submit it if not
proposals.body:
## Problem
LobeHub's MCP marketplace (lobehub.com/mcp redirects to market.lobehub.com) ranks servers by install count, rating and stars. No issue covers it yet. The page asks clients to register with `npx -y @lobehub/market-cli register` before `mcp search`. We have not checked whether vn-skills or any Vietnam server is listed there, and we have not found a submission process.

Source: https://lobehub.com/mcp?q=vietnam

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Search the marketplace for `vn-skills` and `vietnam` (web UI or `@lobehub/market-cli`). Note the results here.
- [ ] If it is listed: check that the description covers all 11 skills and links to the current npm package.
- [ ] If it is not listed: find LobeHub's submission docs and submit, using the README description. Say it is offline and needs no credentials, as in the mcp.so issue (#196).
- [ ] Post the listing URL here and close the issue.
proposals.rationale: [needs you] The project has 0 stars, so it needs discovery through directories. This is a channel nobody has checked yet, and checking it is cheap.
